# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`** 与 [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta) 同属 **0.3.0 正式版前的预发布版本**：在既有 JiuwenSwarm 科研工作台能力之上，继续收敛质量与工程化交付，为正式版做候选验证。

上一版本为 `0.3.0-beta`（2026-09-30）。本版本汇总 **2026-10-01 → 2026-10-16**（Asia/Shanghai）已合并进 `main` 的变更。

> 本文是面向社区征求意见的 **Release Note 草案**，不是正式发版公告；正式 GitHub Release / tag 将另发。

## Release Note 草案

### 新功能

- **L1–L5 多级 CI 门禁**：按 PR → merge → daily → release 分层累积质量检查，Nightly/Release 真实 E2E 与 hermetic 检查并行落地（#259，相关 #280、#255、#258）。

### 主要修复

- **沙箱 / Runner 未就绪**：启动与 Runner 就绪解耦；执行仍 fail-closed；Agent 可通过 `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` 等待，并弹出重试/切换/取消恢复卡片；区分「展示等待」与「授权修复」（#275 / #265，#282）。
- **不可解析 tool call**：长科研 run 中改为扣留并恢复，不再误报为模型配置错误并整段结束主/子 Agent（#247 / #236）。
- **自定义模型设置**：任一设置接口失败时保留 provider 预设，避免 Custom provider 空表单卡死（#288 / #281）。
- **交付签收**：接受带可选章节号的 Methods/Results/References，避免临近预算误触发重写（#294 / #292）。
- **产物提交**：CAS ref commit 复用已校验对象元数据，降低长轨迹提交开销（#250；#230 仍开）。
- **真实 E2E 稳定化**：J5 等待托管 Python（#287 / #286）；主 Agent run 链完成后再做终局断言（#253）；中断时保留已完成旅程证据（#266 / #263）；Nightly flaky 断言（#207、#279）；L3 改为真实用户旅程（#272）。
- **CI 配套**：job 重跑覆盖同名 artifact（#302 / #301）；分数与诊断产物分离（#240）；Mock E2E 四 worker、UT 并行等（#273、#277、#268、#242）；Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 恢复进 daily/release，Nightly 结构化挂载 `science-research-team`（#270、#306）。

### 行为变更

- 启动不再强依赖本地沙箱可用；未就绪时执行被拒绝，需经恢复流程后再下发（#275）。
- Nightly Biomni 挂载 `science-research-team` 后，分数不可与 beta 裸题基线直接对比（#306）。

## 社区反馈

欢迎在本 Issue 讨论：

- 草案表述是否清楚、是否遗漏重要合入

# English version

## Release positioning

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`**, like [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta), is a **pre-release ahead of the formal 0.3.0**. It builds on the existing JiuwenSwarm scientific workbench and continues to tighten quality and delivery engineering as a release candidate.

The previous version is `0.3.0-beta` (2026-09-30). This draft covers changes merged into `main` from **2026-10-01 through 2026-10-16** (Asia/Shanghai).

> This is a **community draft** for feedback, not a formal release announcement. The GitHub Release / tag will be published separately.

## Draft release notes

### New features

- **L1–L5 multi-level CI gates**: layered quality checks across PR → merge → daily → release, with Nightly/Release real E2E alongside hermetic checks (#259; related #280, #255, #258).

### Major fixes

- **Sandbox / Runner not ready**: decouple workbench startup from Runner readiness; execution remains fail-closed; the Agent can wait via `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` and present retry / switch / cancel recovery cards; distinguish “show waiting UI” from “authorize repair” (#275 / #265, #282).
- **Unparseable tool calls**: hold and recover during long research runs instead of misreporting a model-configuration error and killing the main or sub-Agent (#247 / #236).
- **Custom model settings**: keep provider presets when any settings request fails, avoiding a stuck empty Custom provider form (#288 / #281).
- **Deliverable acceptance**: accept Methods/Results/References headings with optional section numbers so near-budget rewrites are not triggered incorrectly (#294 / #292).
- **Artifact commits**: reuse validated object metadata on the CAS ref-commit path to cut long-trajectory commit cost (#250; #230 remains open).
- **Real E2E stabilization**: wait for managed Python on J5 (#287 / #286); assert only after the main Agent run chain completes (#253); retain completed-journey evidence on interrupt (#266 / #263); Nightly flaky assertions (#207, #279); L3 as real user journeys (#272).
- **CI follow-ups**: overwrite same-named artifacts on job re-run (#302 / #301); separate score and diagnostic artifacts (#240); Mock E2E four workers and UT parallelism (#273, #277, #268, #242); restore Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 to daily/release and structurally attach `science-research-team` on Nightly (#270, #306).

### Behavior changes

- Startup no longer requires a ready local sandbox; execution is rejected until recovery completes (#275).
- After Nightly Biomni attaches `science-research-team`, scores are not directly comparable to the beta bare-prompt baseline (#306).

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

In multi-step science demos, the agent repeatedly hits **tool-call failures** that it then recovers from on retry. Tasks still complete, but the timeline fills with failed cards and wasted turns. Two concrete patterns showed up in Scenario 2/3.

## Repro / observations

### A. Specialist `task` missing required prompt (Scenario 2 Case B)

1. Create custom specialist **CSV质检专员** bound to skill `csv-quality-check`.
2. Start a session with that specialist selected; upload CSV; ask for a quality check **without** naming the skill.
3. Parent `read_skill` completes; first `task` **fails** (missing required prompt field); retry **completes** with `specialistId` and skill path.
4. Subagent eventually COMPLETED; parent re-checks and declares artifacts.

Session `378644b7-…`, project **自定义扩展演示**.

### B. lmfit `conf_interval` signature (Scenario 3 Case A)

1. Domain-allowlist sandbox; `environment_create` task env; `environment_install` lmfit **1.3.4** from PyPI.
2. Fit Michaelis–Menten; two `run_python` calls **fail** on lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention; later calls succeed after the agent fixes the call.
3. Final fit OK (Vmax/Km/R²), but timeline shows two failed Python cards.

Session `ae359b61-…`, project **科学计算演示**, 2026-10-16.

Similar soft failures also appeared in Scenario 1 (`run_shell` / `run_python` fail-then-complete).

## Expected

- Specialist delegation: first `task` payload should always include required fields (prompt) when the product launches a specialist subagent — schema/validation before the card is shown as failed.
- Scientific library helpers: either pin known-good call patterns in skills/examples, or catch common `conf_interval` / API mismatches with a clearer error that steers the next call without two opaque failures.
- Prefer failing closed in the UI with a one-line “retrying with fixed args” rather than raw failed tool cards as the default narrative.

## Actual

Runs complete via model self-repair, but users see multiple **failed** tool cards and longer wall time for routine fits / specialist handoffs.

## Priority

**Medium** — reliability / polish of the tool loop; not a hard blocker when Always-allow is on.

## Related

- #330 — engineering-heavy timeline makes these failures more alarming than they are
- #327 — long runs already lack incremental progress
items.title: [Bug]: Agent tool calls fail then recover mid-run (task missing prompt; lmfit conf_interval signature)

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

Uploading a PDF through the workspace **Drop files** control does not go through the paper-reader pipeline. Paper reader stays at **0 parsed**, and the agent only sees a raw file (often with almost no extractable scientific content unless it scrapes bytes itself).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, new session in a data-analysis project.
2. Drop `experiment_notes.pdf` (+ optional CSV) via **Drop files**.
3. Ask the agent to read the PDF notes and fit kinetics from the CSV (no network).
4. Observe: Paper reader counter remains **0 parsed**. Agent reports extracting only the single plain line from the PDF and explicitly notes missing protocol/units/replicates. Units come from the CSV header, not from structured paper parse.

Observed Scenario 1 Case B (session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**), 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Dropping a PDF into the workspace should either:
  - enqueue it for paper-reader parsing (same as the dedicated paper input), **or**
  - clearly label the upload as “file only / not paper-parsed” so users do not assume literature extraction ran.
- If Drop files is intentionally file-only, the empty/paper UI should not imply paper intake for that artifact.

## Actual

PDF is a workspace file only. Paper reader stays **0 parsed**. Structured literature extraction does not run on Drop-files PDFs.

## Priority

**Medium–High** for any “upload paper + analyze” flow; easy to misread as a successful paper ingest.

## Related

Not the same as empty-session CSV intro (#328). Speaks to intake path consistency between Drop files and paper-reader.
items.title: [Bug]: PDF uploaded via Drop files is not parsed by Paper reader (0 parsed)

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

The workspace **Artifacts** list appears **project-scoped**: while working in session B, files from session A in the same project still show up (sometimes grouped under the other session’s name). Not a data-loss bug — the model still read the correct uploads — but the list is noisy and easy to mis-click.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 demos:

- Scenario 1: session B’s file count included session A artifacts.
- Scenario 2: during Specialist session, Case A reports still listed under “Skill csv-quality-check” while new files appeared under “Specialist CSV质检”.

## Why this may be intentional

Project-level sharing can be desirable (reuse a CSV across sessions, compare outputs). This issue is filed **low priority** to force an explicit product decision, not to demand an immediate change.

## Design questions (need a call)

1. Should Artifacts default to **current session only**, with an opt-in “Show project files”?
2. Or keep project scope but visually separate **This session** vs **Other sessions** with clearer hierarchy?
3. Should uploads be session-private by default and only promoted to project library on pin/share?

## Expected after a design pass

Whatever the choice, the panel should make scope obvious so users do not think another session’s outputs belong to the active run.

## Priority

**Low** — polish / information architecture; confirm against intended project-workspace model before changing.

## Related

Not a substitute for timeline density (#330).
items.title: Usability (low): workspace Artifacts panel is project-scoped and mixes other sessions’ files

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Problem

Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain literal `<think>` tags.

These tags appear as part of the visible title instead of a clean summary of the conversation. This makes session titles confusing and harder to scan.

The issue is intermittent; the exact trigger has not yet been identified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session and send a message.
2. Wait for the session title to be automatically generated.
3. Check the generated title.
4. Occasionally, the title contains literal `<think>` tags.

### Actual behavior

The generated session title includes `<think>` markup.

### Expected behavior

Automatically generated session titles should contain only a concise, readable summary of the conversation, without reasoning tags or reasoning content.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Automatically generated titles never display `<think>` or `</think>` tags.
- [ ] Reasoning content enclosed by these tags is excluded from the title.
- [ ] If no usable title remains after filtering, the application retains a safe default title.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes title-generation responses containing reasoning tags.
items.title: [Bug]: Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain `<think>` tags

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Problem

Users face two obstacles when downloading ScienceDiscovery:

1. **Release downloads are difficult to discover.** Installation packages are listed under **Assets** on the GitHub Releases page. When this section is collapsed, users may miss the downloads or struggle to find the package for their platform.
2. **The website installation page lacks a version selector and defaults to an outdated version.** Version 0.3 is available, but the installation page still defaults to 0.2. Users cannot select a release version directly on the page and may install an older version unintentionally.

### Proposed improvements

**GitHub Releases**

- Add a clearly visible download section to each release description, with direct links to installation packages.
- Label each download by operating system and architecture so users can identify the appropriate package without expanding Assets.

**Website installation page**

- Add a version selector so users can choose between available releases.
- Default to the latest stable release, currently 0.3.
- Keep download links and installation commands consistent with the selected version.
- Update the default version when a new stable release becomes available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can find installation package links in the release description without expanding Assets.
- [ ] Download links clearly identify the supported operating system and architecture.
- [ ] The website installation page provides a version selector.
- [ ] The installation page defaults to the latest stable release.
- [ ] Download links and installation commands match the selected version.
- [ ] Publishing a new stable release updates the website’s default installation version.
items.title: [Bug]: Release downloads are hard to find and the website installation page defaults to an outdated version

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_
items.title: [Feature]: Natural-language program evolution: turn /evolve-design from a hidden slash command into a framework-recommended, natural-language interaction

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What is wrong

On a large screen the artifact viewer is still a small card. It is the dialog opened from an artifact (`artifact-modal-panel` in `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css`):

- width `min(1080px, 100%)`
- only a max height, `calc(100vh - 56px)`, so a short file stays as short as its content

On a 1920px-wide window that width is about 56% of the viewport. On a 2560px window it is about 42%. Plots, tables, notebooks, and source previews then sit in a column that does not use the screen the user is looking at.

The same class is the shell for the evidence viewer and the node-detail viewer (`ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, `EvidenceModal.tsx`, `DetailModal.tsx`). They should grow with it. Confirmation dialogs and settings panels use other classes and stay small.

## What a reasonable size is

A decision dialog and a content viewer are different objects.

- Material’s dialog cap (560dp wide, 48dp from the screen edge) is for a question or a confirmation. Applying it here would make the viewer smaller.
- A content viewer should take most of the viewport and leave a visible margin, so the dimmed page and the click-outside close still read as a layer. A hard pixel cap still matters on a 4K display, or a paragraph becomes one very long line.
- WorkBuddy opens an artifact as a tab in the right-hand pane, and that pane can go fullscreen. This product’s right pane is 390px, which is too narrow to become the viewer. Growing the existing dialog is the change; do not move artifact viewing into that pane.
- This repo already treats specialized viewers as large windows: the CSV workspace is `min(1480px, 97vw)` by `min(920px, 95vh)` (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/styles.css`), and the molecule window is `min(1360px, 96vw)` by `min(880px, 93vh)`. The generic artifact dialog is the one that did not follow that pattern.

## Target

On a wide screen, size the artifact viewer like those content windows, one step larger:

- width `min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`
- height `min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`

That is 1600×960 when the window is large enough, and it shrinks with an 80px total margin when it is not. It does not go edge to edge. At `max-width: 900px` the existing rule already makes this panel full viewport; leave that rule alone.

Inside the window, prose stays readable. Markdown body copy keeps a measure of about 76ch. Tables, code, images, and plots use the window width. Do not widen a paragraph to 1600px.

The evidence title already ellipsizes at `min(560px, 60vw)`. That cap can stay. The comment above it still says the panel is about 1080px; update the comment if that block is touched.

## Out of scope

- Settings, creation, and deletion dialogs.
- The CSV workspace and the molecule window. They are already larger than 1080px.
- The 390px workspace panel.
- The conversation column width.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width of about 1920px, the artifact viewer is 1600px wide and 960px tall, centered, with the page still visible around it.
- At a width between 900px and 1600px, the viewer is the viewport minus about 80px, not stuck at 1080px.
- At 900px and below, the viewer is still the full viewport, as it is today.
- A markdown artifact’s paragraphs do not run the full 1600px. A wide table or source preview does use the window.
- Evidence and node-detail viewers use the same size. A settings dialog does not.
- A render test, or a CSS assertion next to the existing dialog styles, locks the new width and height.
items.title: [Feature]: Make the artifact viewer use a large screen

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What to change

On a large screen the Session conversation is too narrow, and it sits on the left. The composer under it is a different width. User messages should be a bubble on the right.

This is layout only. Do not change what a message contains, the right-hand artifact panel, or the narrow-screen stacking behavior.

## Current layout

The conversation pane is the left track of `.content-grid` (`apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`). The right track is a fixed 390px panel.

Inside the conversation pane:

- Each `.message` and the run timeline are capped at `820px` and are not centered, so on a wide pane they stay on the left. The same `820px` cap is repeated for the message skeleton, process records, and several timeline blocks (`conversation.css`, `timeline.css`, `process-records.css`, `feedback.css`).
- The composer does not use that cap. It stretches across the pane with `margin: 0 max(28px, 5vw) 28px`, so on a large screen it is wider than the transcript above it.
- A user turn is the same left grid as an assistant turn: a 40px avatar column, then the body. `.message.user .markdown-body` is only an inline block with a sunk background. It is not on the right.

## What other agents do

Public pages do not publish a single official pixel width. The pattern that matches this request:

- **Doubao (doubao.com).** The transcript and the input share one centered column (`--center-content-max-width`, `--content-max-width`, `--chat-area-max-width` on the chat route). The column stays centered in the area beside the left navigation as the window grows; it is not the full window. User sends are a separate right-aligned bubble. Community style scripts refer to a stock send-message cap around `max-w-650`, and they right-align that bubble with `margin-left: auto`. The stock column is what people widen with userscripts; one width slider starts at 760px, another forces 1600px. Those overrides are “make it full width,” which is not what we want. A public recreation of the Doubao column uses `max-width: 1000px`.
- **WorkBuddy.** The published UI is a left task list, a center conversation, and an optional right results panel. The input sits at the bottom of that same center column, so the transcript and the input are one width. The docs do not give a pixel width or say which side a user message sits on.
- **Trae.** Side chat is the IDE panel on the right (Command+U / Ctrl+U). Its width is the panel the user drags, not a centered reading column. It is a poor template for this screen.

## Target

On a wide conversation pane, one centered column holds the transcript and the composer. Make it a little wider than 820px, and do not let it fill the pane.

Use **1000px** as the shared max width (`min(1000px, 100%)`, centered with `margin-inline: auto`). That is the modest step implied by “a little wider,” and it matches the 1000px Doubao-style column rather than the 1600px full-width userscripts. Put the number in one custom property and point the transcript, timeline, process records, skeleton, and composer at it, so the old `820px` copies cannot drift apart.

The composer’s outer width is that column. Its inner padding can stay. Short viewports keep today’s full-width behavior, including the ~900px case where the sidebar must not cover the conversation.

User messages, inside that column:

- The bubble sits on the right.
- A short message is only as wide as its text. A long message wraps and may use the column width, but it still starts from the right.
- Assistant replies stay on the left and use the column width.
- Do not leave the user avatar in the left gutter while the bubble is on the right. Keep the avatar with the bubble, or drop the user avatar if it fights the bubble. Assistant avatars stay on the left.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width where the conversation pane is clearly wider than 1000px, the transcript and the composer are the same width, centered in the pane, and that width is 1000px rather than 820px or the full pane.
- A short user message is a bubble on the right of that column. An assistant message stays on the left.
- Below the width of the column, the column fills the pane and the composer still matches it. The existing narrow layout, including the sidebar at about 900px, still fits on the first screen.
- The right artifact panel stays 390px.
- A Web layout test or the existing conversation render test covers the shared column and the right-aligned user bubble.
items.title: [Feature]: Center a wider conversation column and right-align user bubbles

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Motivation

Currently, every conversation must belong to a project, and creating a project requires too much configuration before users can start chatting.

This adds friction to the first interaction: users who simply want to ask a question or explore an idea must first create and configure a project, even when they do not yet need one. It also encourages creating projects for one-off conversations, making project management unnecessarily cluttered.

Users should be able to open the application and start a conversation immediately, then organize their work into projects when needed.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make project membership optional for conversations.**
   - Provide a prominent “New chat” entry that works without creating or selecting a project.
   - Support standalone conversations for quick questions, exploration, and one-off tasks.
   - Keep project-based conversations available for ongoing research and related work.

2. **Allow users to organize conversations into projects later.**
   - Let users move a standalone conversation into a new or existing project.
   - Preserve conversation history and associated artifacts when moving it.
   - Make it clear whether a conversation belongs to a project.

3. **Simplify project creation.**
   - Require only the minimum information needed to create a project, such as its name.
   - Provide sensible defaults and make advanced configuration optional.
   - Allow users to update project settings later instead of requiring them before the first conversation.

4. **Provide clear navigation for both workflows.**
   - Make standalone conversations and projects easy to find.
   - Let users start a conversation directly from the main interface.
   - Within a project, let users create conversations associated with that project.

## Example user flows

### Start chatting immediately

Open the application → New chat → Send a message.

No project creation or project configuration is required.

### Organize an exploratory conversation

Start a standalone conversation → Decide to continue the work → Move the conversation into a new or existing project.

### Start with a project

Create a project with minimal information → Start a conversation → Configure additional project settings when needed.

## Questions to settle

- Should standalone conversations remain in chat history by default, with an explicitly ephemeral mode handled separately?
- Which project settings can use defaults, and which are genuinely required before a project-specific capability runs?
- When an existing conversation moves into a project, how should project context and settings apply to subsequent messages?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with no projects can open the application and send a first message without creating or configuring a project.
- [ ] Users can create and continue conversations outside projects.
- [ ] Users can still create conversations directly within a project.
- [ ] A standalone conversation can be moved into a new or existing project without losing its history or associated artifacts.
- [ ] Project creation requires only minimal information; advanced settings can be configured later.
- [ ] Navigation clearly distinguishes standalone conversations from project conversations.
- [ ] Existing projects and their conversations remain accessible.
- [ ] E2E coverage verifies starting a conversation with no projects, creating a project with minimal input, and moving a standalone conversation into a project.
items.title: [Feature]: Allow conversations outside projects and simplify project creation

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
Follow-up discovered during the repository-wide review of #295; related to #288 and #291. Suggested priority: **P2**.

A failed model connection can silently undo a successful settings change made by another tab or API client while the connection test is running. The wizard restores the entire global-settings snapshot captured before the attempt, including fields it did not change.

This is **pre-existing**, not a regression introduced by #295. The same browser/API reproduction failed on both the base commit `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310` and PR revision `45366a904edc7c57e69d36ce79b944e75b382d45`. The rollback code remains unchanged in the latest PR revision `d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635`.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated instance, the real API/store, and a local model endpoint that returns an authentication failure. No real provider credentials are needed.

1. Start with no registered models and persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
2. Open System settings → Models and connect a custom provider. Let the wizard successfully read global settings, create the provider, and register its first model. The backend automatically selects this first model as the global default.
3. While `POST /api/models/:id/test` is pending, use a second API client to read the current overrides and successfully write them back with only `thinkingEffort` changed to `"low"`. Preserve the current temporary `modelId` in this write.
4. Let the connection test return an authentication failure.
5. Read back `GET /api/settings`.

Observed interleaving, with the generated model ID abbreviated:

| Stage | Persisted overrides |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state / wizard snapshot | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |
| Successful concurrent write | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"low","modelId":"temporary-model"}` |
| Wizard rollback | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |

**Actual:** the concurrent `"low"` setting is silently replaced by the old `"high"` value.

**Expected:** undo only this attempt's default-model change when it is still owned by the attempt; preserve the other client's `"low"` setting and every other unrelated override.

The browser reproduction intercepts the model-test request only to schedule a second, successful write through the real settings API before allowing the failing model test to proceed. It uses the actual App, wizard, HTTP API, and store.

## Cause and implementation boundary

[`ModelConnectWizard.restoreSavedOverrides`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L360-L377) calls `replaceGlobalSettings(savedOverrides)` on failure. This replaces the whole settings object with a snapshot taken before provider creation and model testing.

The backend needs the attempt's automatic default cleared before it can delete the temporary model, but restoring unrelated fields is unnecessary. The same unconditional rollback also runs when existing models meant the attempt did not change the default.

The [documented settings boundary](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md#L220-L232) already provides a catalog-level settings mutex and revision-checked plugin writes. Classic PUT intentionally remains last-writer-wins. This issue concerns the wizard's stale whole-object compensation; it does not require changing all classic PUT semantics.

A frontend-only fresh GET followed by another whole-object PUT still leaves a read/write race. Use an atomic conditional undo or equivalent version/ownership check at the existing server-side settings boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed connection preserves unrelated global-setting changes committed while that connection is in progress, including explicit empty connector selections.
- [ ] Rollback changes `modelId` only if the current default still belongs to this attempt; a newer default chosen by another writer is not overwritten.
- [ ] If the attempt never changed the global default, cleanup does not restore the old global-settings snapshot.
- [ ] In the uncontended first-model failure case, the temporary automatic default is safely undone and only the attempt's provider/models are deleted; existing references remain protected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic integration regression test using real settings persistence and an interleaved second writer. Check persisted settings after rollback and reopening the store, rather than only asserting mock delete calls.
- [ ] Cover both an unrelated-field edit and a concurrent default-model change, while retaining #295's test that a failed initial settings read creates no provider/model.

This is separate from #291: here the wizard's initial settings read succeeds, and the loss occurs during later failure rollback after another writer has saved successfully.
items.title: [Bug]: Model connection rollback overwrites concurrent global settings changes

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## Environment

- Release package `sciencediscovery` **0.3.0-beta** (x86_64), started with `ScienceDiscovery serve`, Linux

## Symptom

Soon after startup the right-side task panel in the web UI shows `invalid internal token`, and the **Retry** button never recovers — the same error returns every time. Chat and agent runs work normally.

## What the shipped package does

1. The payload contains no evolve sidecar, and the launcher neither starts one nor passes `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` / `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the API (confirmed in the running API process' environment). Memory-graph gets the opposite treatment — the launcher seeds it with a per-run random token (`services/launcher/src/memory-graph.ts:27`).
2. With both variables unset the API falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:4313` with the constant token `sciencediscovery-evolve-local` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/config.ts:253-256`).
3. Whatever process happens to hold `127.0.0.1:4313` therefore receives the API's evolve traffic. In my case that port was held by another process running an evolve sidecar configured with its own token, so the calls came back `401 {"detail":"invalid internal token"}` — and the frontend relayed that raw `detail` string into the task panel, where Retry just re-issues the same call.

I verified the error did not come from my own stack's memory-graph: the launcher-generated token matches the API's on both sides, and its access log shows zero 401s. The string is in fact the loopback-auth rejection detail shared by both sidecars (`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/auth.py:40`, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/auth.py:40`) — which is why it reaches users with no hint of which service or token failed.

## Why the fallback itself is the problem

- The API ends up calling an arbitrary process that happens to bind a fixed port, authenticating with a token guessable from the public source. A sidecar that rejects it produces the unrecoverable raw error above; a process that accepts it (or runs an evolve sidecar with the token unset — auth is permissive then) would be silently used by this installation.
- Run specifications sent to the sidecar carry the LLM proxy URL and token (`llm`, `judge` fields in `services/api/src/evolution/sidecar.ts`), so whatever holds the port also receives those credentials.

## Suggestions

- Give evolve the same launcher treatment as memory-graph: start it from the payload with a per-run random token, or explicitly disable it / point the API at an operator-configured URL, so the constant fallback is never reached.
- When a sidecar call fails, report which sidecar failed instead of relaying the raw `detail` to the UI.
- Prefer per-installation fallback credentials over source constants, and avoid fixed default sidecar ports (related: #267).

Workaround I applied locally: launch with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` pointing at an unused loopback port, so the API no longer calls whatever holds 4313.
items.title: Hardcoded evolve sidecar fallback (127.0.0.1:4313 + fixed token) surfaces raw "invalid internal token" in the UI

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Strengthen the existing L1–L5 gates so that core scientific features have explicit regression protection, and introduce the full, version-pinned BiomniBench-DA suite as an L5 capability non-regression gate. Keep the existing shared catalog, frozen plans, candidate-SHA/backend identity checks, and exact execution accounting.

BiomniBench-DA should measure data-analysis capability; it must not be treated as complete coverage of Idea Tree, remote execution, provenance, Reviewer, or upgrade/recovery behavior. Those features need dedicated acceptance cases.

This is a follow-up implementation plan to #248. Its pre-merge L5 certification proposal is an explicit policy extension beyond the original release-only L5 scope. Related prerequisites: #252 (wait for the complete Biomni execution/wake chain before checking delivery) and #245 (endpoint latency and empty-terminal-turn diagnostics). Reuse those investigations rather than duplicate them. The source review used commit `e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215`; counts below describe that snapshot, not newly executed CI results. Reconcile with current main before implementation. GitHub rulesets and Environment settings were not verified in this review.

## Current coverage and gaps

- L3 declares nine real cases: response, tool, files, memory, artifact, workspace, cancellation, and two Runner wait/finish recovery cases.
- L4/L5 currently select the same 19 real identities: those nine plus five DRB cases, Research Team, PUCT compression, J5 statistics, and two run/artifact-card provenance journeys. There is no eligible L5-only increment.
- Idea Tree is **not untested**: it has Python/API/package tests and a mocked browser journey covering pause/resume, three rounds, independent assessments, persistence, and termination. The browser fixture supplies one candidate per round and fixed scores; it does not establish real-model research quality or realistic multi-branch exploration.
- Existing Reviewer and literature tests already cover several evidence, identity, lifecycle, and failure contracts. Extend their missing boundaries rather than duplicate them.
- BiomniBench-DA currently has two quarantined cases using a local rubric judge adapter. Evaluation errors are recorded as non-gating, and there is no capability threshold.
- The migration ledger lists 77 Neo4j external identities and 17 unreviewed delegation identities. Map existing replacement coverage before reinstating or retiring individual cases.
- Some public-API journeys have standalone commands but are not wired into the shared CI plan.

## L5: full BiomniBench-DA capability certification

- [ ] Define a versioned manifest for the complete intended BiomniBench-DA release: task IDs, authorized data assets/checksums, instructions, evaluator/grader version, generator and judge configuration, tools, budgets, and attempts. Missing prerequisites must not silently shrink the suite.
- [ ] Repair the current isolated-task prerequisites, then expand beyond the two existing cases to the complete manifest. Record all exclusions explicitly; do not label an incomplete run as full-suite certification.
- [ ] Decide and name the evaluation protocol. The current local rubric adapter is not the upstream Gemini verifier; scores from different protocols/judges must not be silently compared or presented as equivalent official scores.
- [ ] Emit separate `delivery`, `evaluation`, and `capability` verdicts. Required evaluation errors, missing scores, non-finite values, or mismatched identities prevent certification. Optional disabled audits must be explicitly N/A.
- [ ] Define product-failure scoring up front. Generation failures, timeouts, and missing answers cannot disappear from the denominator. Infrastructure/judge failures must remain visible as blocked/incomplete certification, not be silently converted to successful results.
- [ ] Establish an approved baseline with per-task results. Freeze comparable backend/model/judge/data/grader/tool/budget identities; do not compare against an ever-moving baseline that can gradually regress.
- [ ] Calibrate a non-inferiority rule and tolerable regression margin using repeated measurements. Preserve all attempts, use a predefined repetition/review policy, and prohibit retry-until-green or best-of-unreported-attempts reporting.
- [ ] Inspect overall capability, task-category regressions, execution success rate, and severe per-task failures. Track latency, resource usage, and cost separately from answer quality.
- [ ] Bind the verdict and retained evidence to the actual candidate SHA and relevant asset hashes. Reuse certification only when the entire declared execution identity remains applicable.
- [ ] Retain dedicated acceptance cases for core features outside DA benchmark coverage, plus previous-release-to-candidate upgrade/read/continue validation where supported.

### Required trigger decision: merge gate versus release gate

The current L5 workflow is triggered after a version tag; that can block publication but cannot prevent a regression from entering main. The intended outcome here includes **pre-merge capability protection**.

- [ ] Make L5 certification callable for the final merge candidate (or a deliberately formed merge batch), and require its verdict before that candidate enters main. A rebuilt candidate must not reuse incompatible evidence.
- [ ] Retain release-time asset checks; reuse an earlier certification only with an explicit matching-identity policy.
- [ ] Document queue latency, concurrency, budget, and failure-localization behavior. If the chosen policy runs only on selected changes or only nightly, state the weaker guarantee explicitly rather than claiming every merge is fully benchmark-certified.

## L4: prioritized real scientific journeys

Priority applies to the **new L4 coverage**, not to removal of existing tests. P0 is the first implementation tranche; P1 follows once completeness and budget controls are available.

| Priority | Feature / proposed case | Observable acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | **Idea Tree: multi-branch, multi-round research with an independently computable evaluator** | Generate distinct candidates; reject hard-constraint violations; execute candidates where applicable; preserve lineage; propagate prior insights into later rounds; select a valid result using independent evidence. Do not require every exploratory round to improve monotonically. |
| **P0** | **Reviewer: paired correct and deliberately flawed reports** | Detect unsupported citations, numeric/unit errors, and evidence from the wrong run/version; avoid false accusations on correct reports; return inconclusive when evidence is insufficient. Measure false positives as well as missed defects. |
| **P0** | **Scientific calculation / J5: fixed-data analysis with an independent numerical oracle** | Persist reproducible computation and verify report values, units, and evidence against independently calculated expectations, rather than merely requiring a Markdown artifact. |
| **P1** | **Literature research: retrieval → acquisition → extraction → citation → report** | Verify source identity and evidence support; exercise representative live connector/PDF paths with bounded budgets. Keep deterministic source/failure fixtures in L2 and distinguish provider availability from product defects. |
| **P1** | **Multi-agent research: successful, failed, and delayed child tasks** | Preserve task/result identity; surface partial failure; propagate cancellation; avoid duplicate dispatch and missing results; prevent an unsupported “all succeeded” final conclusion. Extend existing Research Team coverage. |
| **P1** | **Evolve/PUCT: independently evaluated candidate optimization** | Verify candidate/parent/baseline identity, legitimate selection, and validation/test separation; invalid or failed evaluations cannot win. Keep seed-as-best valid; do not require arbitrary improvement in every run. |

For all cases, enter through the product's public interfaces, record model/backend identity and usage, enforce explicit execution budgets, and retain auditable evidence. Generating a score is not itself a passing capability verdict.

## L1–L3: close engineering and integration gaps

### L1: trustworthy policy and manifests

- [ ] Add independent validation of CI-sensitive changes against a trusted base. A change must not weaken selectors/gates and their self-tests together without detection; legitimate policy changes need an explicit review path. Unknown impact must fail or fall back to the full intended plan.
- [ ] Validate benchmark manifest schema, unique IDs, frozen inputs, required evaluation fields, and explicit exclusions.
- [ ] Restore appropriate dependency-vulnerability, secret, and static-security checks that are not replaced by the current test gate.
- [ ] Verify repository administration separately: required `merge-gate`, Merge Queue, current-head review/stale-approval dismissal, and permitted Environment refs. YAML presence is not proof that these are enforced.

### L2: deterministic product and scientific contracts

- [ ] Register suitable existing public-API journeys in the shared catalog, especially remote execution wake-up, detached Runner behavior, and memory/provenance journeys. Preserve isolated processes/data and planned/executed accounting.
- [ ] Add a reproducible temporary Neo4j integration job for the applicable external identities; local-backend tests are not a substitute for Neo4j behavior.
- [ ] Map the 17 unreviewed delegation identities to current Swarm coverage; restore missing behaviors or explicitly document verified replacements.
- [ ] Extend Idea Tree mocked E2E to multiple branches with good, weak, and invalid candidates, pruning, failure recovery, and final selection assertions.
- [ ] Test evaluation aggregation with injected judge timeouts, missing/invalid scores, wrong versions, and missing tasks. No incomplete evaluation may produce full certification.
- [ ] Test suite request/token budget enforcement, including retries, children, judges, cancellation, and unknown usage. Existing context or feature-local budgets do not establish a suite-wide cost ceiling.
- [ ] Extend literature/Reviewer fixtures with wrong pages, unsupported citations, unit errors, cross-session/version evidence, and correct counterexamples. Consider sanitized HTTP replay with CI auto-recording disabled; keep online freshness checks separate.
- [ ] Verify remote success and recovery: input transfer, execution in separate storage, artifact return, completion wake-up, no duplicate execution after reconnect, and no orphan work after cancellation.
- [ ] Verify full provenance from input version through code/environment/execution to report; same-named files in different sessions must not mix, and old reports must not silently point to new versions.
- [ ] Audit existing process-recovery tests and add missing actual API/Runner/Swarm restart journeys. Browser refresh and session reopening do not establish server recovery.

### L3: small real-model and distribution acceptance

- [ ] Add a bounded real-model smoke for critical feature entry points such as Idea Tree; leave deep research and quality evaluation to L4/L5.
- [ ] Exercise critical upload → execution → artifact-read behavior against the actual distribution candidate. Preserve the existing two-architecture binary and Docker gates and publish the assets that were tested.
- [ ] Apply explicit paid-call budgets to the merge-candidate suite without weakening identity or failure accounting.

## Follow-up coverage audits

- [ ] Define supported-platform obligations before adding macOS, real SSH, NPU, R, or additional dependency matrices. Do not infer coverage from Linux/amd64 tests or arm64 boot smoke.
- [ ] Audit long-running concurrency, process cleanup, and upgrade/migration tests before adding duplicates.
- [ ] Maintain a feature × tier × failure-mode coverage map linked to case IDs, so “has unit tests” is not mistaken for “has real scientific acceptance.”
- [ ] Add deduplicated nightly failure tracking, ownership, recovery handling, and sufficient release-evidence retention.

## Completion criteria and rollout

1. Make results trustworthy first: frozen manifests, evaluation-completeness contracts, budget controls, baseline protocol, and required-check configuration.
2. Bring suitable existing journeys and external integration tests into routine CI; resolve delegation coverage mapping.
3. Land L4 P0 cases, then P1 enhancements, reusing existing fixtures and assertions where appropriate.
4. Enable full L5 certification on the intended pre-merge candidate, with calibrated non-regression rules and artifact-bound release evidence.

Acceptance must include deliberate fault injection: a missing selected task, judge failure, invalid winning candidate, mismatched fingerprint, exceeded budget, or weakened selection policy must not produce a green certification. Selection-only checks are not evidence that the complete suite executed successfully.

## Source anchors for the reviewed snapshot

- [Profiles and selection](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs)
- [Tier gate](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/.ci/tier-policy.mjs)
- [CI workflow](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [Existing Idea Tree browser journey](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/journey-idea-tree-fixture.spec.ts)
- [Existing Biomni cases and non-gating evaluation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts)
- [Migration and excluded identities](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/support/tagged/MIGRATION.md)
items.title: 【CI】Strengthen L1–L5 gates with full BiomniBench-DA regression checks and prioritized scientific journeys

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Problem

ScienceDiscovery exposes many settings, but a user working in a conversation often does not know which page or field will unblock the current task. For example, adding a model API can require entering a service URL/key, registering a model, selecting its scope, and returning to the original request. A settings-page wizard for initial model connection was proposed in #39; this issue covers **configuration discovered during a task and completed inside the conversation**.

## Proposed experience

Keep existing valid settings and defaults. When a concrete task is blocked by a supported missing capability, or the user explicitly asks for a change:

1. The Agent explains the need in the context of the task and proposes **one specific change**. It pre-fills facts it knows and asks only for missing fields.
2. An in-conversation card shows the current → proposed value, where a resource will be saved, where it will be used (session/project/global), the target service or file, and any connection test or other external action.
3. The user fills in any remaining URL, credential, supported path, or selection and clicks **“Confirm configuration and continue”** (or declines). This one action confirms the fully visible change and the continuation intent.
4. A trusted configuration service validates, tests as disclosed, applies, and then resumes the task. A validation error remains on the card for correction. The result separately reports **saved**, **effective for the task**, and **task resumed/queued**.

For example: “This image analysis needs a vision-capable model. Add this supported model service with its API URL and key, test the selected model, save the provider in this deployment, and use the model in this session.” If an existing vision model is available, offer a one-click session selection instead.

The normal settings pages remain available for inspection and manual management. A usable default should never trigger a configuration interruption merely because another option might be better.

## V1 scope

- Select an already configured model for the current session.
- Add a model connection through an **already supported provider/protocol**, provide or repair its credential, verify it, and bind a selected model to the session. Creating a provider resource does **not** silently change the global default.
- Enable an installed, already configured connector for the session. Its later tool calls still follow the existing execution-permission rules.
- Show the same card without relying on the Agent when no model is configured or the current model's authentication has failed; preserve the user's first task and start it once configuration succeeds.
- Persist card state across refresh/reconnect and continue through a linked follow-up run when the active run's model/tool snapshot must change.

A URL alone must not be treated as a usable arbitrary REST tool. New HTTP/SSE MCP connections, OAuth, controlled file/environment imports, and deployment-wide proxy/timeout changes can follow with dedicated adapters. STDIO commands, host execution, restart-required deployment settings, and arbitrary REST adaptation need separate review.

## Design constraints

- The Agent may inspect a **redacted** capability catalog and create a structured proposal. Only a user-bound decision endpoint may approve it; the Agent must not receive a generic settings-write tool or claim user consent through another tool.
- Secrets use dedicated fields and encrypted backend storage. Plaintext keys must not enter chat messages, model context, tool traces, SSE events, ordinary logs, or browser persistence. A local browser path is not a server path; any supported file import must show the exact environment and read scope.
- Show the real save scope and effective-use scope. Prefer a session override when supported; disclose shared-resource or global effects before confirmation. Do not invent a session-only option for a system-wide setting.
- Bind approval to a proposal revision and concrete target, diff, scope, and verification plan. Re-preview after concurrent setting changes. External probes or reads require explicit disclosure; failed validation must leave the effective configuration intact.
- Do not hot-swap an in-flight run's snapshot by assumption. Finish or stop at a safe boundary, account for pending tools and side effects, then create an idempotent linked continuation using the approved new snapshot. Stop/cancel must suppress automatic continuation. Saved configuration and resumed execution are distinct states.
- An undo action should preview the reverse change and use version checks; it must not overwrite later edits or delete a shared resource still in use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing valid configuration remains unchanged and completes a task without a card.
- [ ] A supported missing model API can be entered, confirmed, verified, saved, and used to continue from the conversation, without visiting settings.
- [ ] Selecting an existing vision model changes only the intended scope; other sessions and global defaults remain unchanged.
- [ ] Invalid credentials do not replace the current working connection; a corrected submission applies once. Supported keyless local endpoints also work.
- [ ] No-model and authentication-failure entry points work without asking a broken model to diagnose itself.
- [ ] Plaintext secrets never appear in messages, events, logs, tool history, or model requests; Agent calls cannot approve a proposal.
- [ ] The displayed resource location, effective scope, target, and possible verification cost match what the backend actually does.
- [ ] Decline/cancel does not repeatedly re-prompt for the same need; a blocked task has a clear reason and any viable alternative.
- [ ] Double-clicks, refresh, SSE replay, retries, and restart recovery create at most one configuration application and one continuation run.
- [ ] Concurrent settings edits make the old proposal stale instead of overwriting the newer value.
- [ ] The old run keeps its historical snapshot; the linked continuation uses the approved new snapshot, preserves the goal and completed artifacts, and does not replay non-idempotent actions.
- [ ] Validation, save, and continuation failures have separate truthful states and phase-specific recovery.
- [ ] Stop, session switching, archival, and deletion cannot apply a proposal in the wrong session or restart a stopped task.
- [ ] Undo restores the former override/inheritance relationship without clobbering subsequent changes or removing a resource used elsewhere.
- [ ] The card supports keyboard use, accessible errors, narrow screens, and Chinese/English text.

## Relation to existing work

#39 addresses a first-connection wizard in settings; this proposal adds task-contextual, Agent-assisted configuration and continuation. The current mainline backend work in #84 (including models/settings #91, chat/runs #89, and MCP #92) should determine the final service and event integration. The product behavior above is the contract; implementation paths and API shapes from the local design draft should be reconciled with current main before coding.

---

## 中文版

### 问题

ScienceDiscovery 有不少设置。用户正在对话里完成任务时，往往不知道哪个页面、哪个字段能够解决眼前的问题。例如接入模型 API，可能要填写服务地址和密钥、注册模型、选择作用范围，再回到原任务。#39 提出的是设置页中的首次模型接入向导；本 Issue 关注的是**任务进行中发现配置缺口，并在对话内完成配置**。

### 期望交互

默认沿用已有的有效配置。只有当前任务确实缺少受支持的能力，或用户主动要求修改时，才进入以下流程：

1. Agent 结合当前任务说明原因，提出**一项明确变更**。已知信息预填，只询问缺少的字段。
2. 对话卡片展示当前值 → 建议值、资源保存位置、实际使用范围（会话／项目／全局）、目标服务或文件，以及即将执行的连接测试等外部动作。
3. 用户补齐必要的地址、凭据、受支持的路径或选择后，点击「确认配置并继续」；也可以拒绝。这一次提交确认的是卡片中完整可见的变更和接续意图。
4. 可信配置服务按卡片说明校验、测试、应用配置，再接续任务。验证失败留在原卡片修正。结果分别说明**配置已保存**、**对任务已生效**、**任务已开始接续或进入队列**，不把三者混为一谈。

例如：「本次图片分析需要支持视觉的模型。请提供受支持的模型服务地址和 API Key；我会测试所选模型，在本部署保存服务，并仅将该模型用于当前会话。」如果已有可用视觉模型，应优先给出一次确认即可完成的会话级选择。

设置页继续作为集中查看和手动维护入口。只要默认配置能完成任务，就不应仅因为存在“更优”选项而打断用户。

### 首版范围

- 为当前会话选择已配置的模型。
- 通过**已有支持的提供方／协议**添加模型连接，补充或修复凭据，验证后把所选模型绑定到会话。新建提供方资源**不等于**悄悄修改全局默认模型。
- 为会话启用已安装、已配置的连接器；之后的实际工具调用仍遵守原有执行权限规则。
- 完全没有模型，或当前模型认证失败时，由确定性的前后端检查显示同类配置卡，不依赖失效模型诊断；保留用户的第一条任务，配置成功后只启动一次。
- 刷新或重连后恢复卡片状态；当前运行的模型或工具快照必须变化时，通过关联的后续运行接续任务。

仅提供一个 URL 不能自动把任意 REST API 变成可调用工具。新建 HTTP/SSE MCP 连接、OAuth、受控文件／环境变量导入，以及部署级代理和超时设置，可在具备专用适配器后逐项扩展。STDIO 命令、宿主执行入口、需要重启的部署设置及任意 REST API 适配需要单独评审。

### 设计边界

- Agent 只能读取**脱敏的**配置能力与状态，并创建结构化提案。只有绑定用户身份的决策接口能够批准；不给 Agent 通用写设置能力，也不能通过其他工具声称「用户已同意」。
- 密钥通过专用字段交给后端并加密保存。明文不得进入聊天消息、模型上下文、工具轨迹、SSE 事件、普通日志或浏览器持久存储。浏览器所在电脑的路径不能当成服务器路径；任何受支持的文件导入都要显示具体运行环境和读取范围。
- 如实展示资源保存范围与最终使用范围。确实支持会话级覆盖时优先只改当前会话；共享资源或全局变更必须提前说明影响。不能给只有系统级设置的项目伪造「仅本会话」选项。
- 用户确认绑定提案版本以及具体目标、差异、范围和验证计划。并发修改导致旧预览过期时应重新预览；外部探测或读取应明确告知；验证失败时保留原有效配置。
- 不能假定进行中的运行可以热切换配置快照。应在安全边界处理未完成的工具和副作用，再用经批准的新快照创建幂等的关联接续运行。用户停止或取消后不得自动接续；配置已保存与任务已继续必须分别记录。
- 「撤销本次配置」应预览反向变更并检查版本，不能覆盖之后的编辑，也不能删除仍被其他会话使用的共享资源。

### 验收标准

- [ ] 已有有效配置能够直接完成任务，不弹配置卡，也不改变原配置。
- [ ] 缺少受支持的模型 API 时，用户可在对话里补齐、确认、验证、保存并接续，无须打开设置页。
- [ ] 选用已有视觉模型时，只修改明确选择的范围；其他会话及全局默认保持不变。
- [ ] 错误凭据不会替换正常连接；修正后只应用一次。受支持的无 Key 本地端点也可使用。
- [ ] 无模型与认证失败都能进入配置流程，无须让失效模型再次诊断自己。
- [ ] 明文凭据不出现在消息、事件、日志、工具历史或模型请求中；Agent 调用不能替用户批准提案。
- [ ] 卡片显示的资源位置、生效范围、目标及可能产生费用的验证动作与后端实际行为一致。
- [ ] 拒绝或取消后不针对同一需求反复打扰；任务受阻时说明原因和可行的替代路径。
- [ ] 双击、刷新、SSE 重放、重试和服务重启至多产生一次配置应用和一个接续运行。
- [ ] 其他窗口修改配置后，旧提案标记为过期并重新预览，不覆盖新值。
- [ ] 旧运行保留历史快照；关联运行使用批准的新快照、原任务目标和已完成产物，不重放已执行的非幂等动作。
- [ ] 验证失败、保存失败和接续失败分别显示真实状态，并提供对应阶段的恢复操作。
- [ ] 停止、切换会话、归档和删除不会在错误会话应用配置，也不会重新启动已停止的任务。
- [ ] 撤销恢复原覆盖或继承关系，不覆盖后续修改，也不删除仍在使用的资源。
- [ ] 卡片支持键盘操作、可访问的错误提示、窄屏布局及中英文文案。

### 与已有工作的关系

#39 聚焦设置页中的首次连接向导；本提案增加任务上下文中的 Agent 协助配置、用户确认和任务接续。主仓当前的后端工作见 #84，其中模型与设置为 #91、对话与运行为 #89、MCP 为 #92。上述产品行为是需要实现的契约；正式开发前，具体服务归属、接口和事件方案应与当前主仓架构核对。

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Summary

When a subagent emits several independent biomedical MCP tool calls in one model response, ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler` executes them one at a time. The workspace registers opaque MCP tools without an `isConcurrencySafe` classifier, so the registry marks them `exclusive` even when JiuwenSwarm submits the requests concurrently. This adds avoidable latency to read-only literature searches. See the 2026-10-12 root-cause comment below for the stage trace and evidence boundary.

### Reproduction

1. Configure a public biomedical MCP source such as PubMed, allowing at least two concurrent source requests.
2. Have a ScienceDiscovery `task` subagent request six independent PubMed MCP searches in one model turn. Test both `allow` and `ask` (approve all six for the latter).
3. Compare the model batch, JiuwenSwarm/MCP SDK request starts, ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` classification, and broker start/end timestamps.

### Observed

In a DA-13-3 local E2E trace, one model SSE summary reported `toolCalls: 6` and `finishReason: tool_calls`. The six approvals were posted close together, but each MCP search started only after the previous search finished. Across the full subagent trace, 49 literature MCP invocations (42 PubMed, 7 Europe PMC) had **zero pairwise execution overlap**; their individual durations summed to 166.6 s. Broker `queueWaitMs` was 0, so its rate/concurrency queue does not explain the serialization. A representative six-call batch took 14.59 s wall time for 12.13 s summed tool execution.

A different DA-13-3 no-subagent trace shows that the main agent's built-in calls can overlap: six `free_search` calls summed to 88.6 s but occupied 21.9 s of union wall time; 24 `fetch_webpage` calls summed to 42.1 s but occupied 15.3 s. These are different tools and workloads, so this is evidence that overlap is possible, **not** a direct speed comparison.

### Expected

Independent read-only calls explicitly classified as concurrency-safe should run concurrently within the source's configured limits. Under `ask`, each call must still receive its own authorization decision; denied calls remain denied.

### Confirmed serialization path

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` does not declare `isConcurrencySafe` for opaque MCP tools. The existing workspace test explicitly checks this default.
- `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` `executionMode` returns `exclusive` when that classifier is absent.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` `ToolScheduler.run` waits for earlier same-batch calls whenever their execution mode is not `parallel`, before the call reaches the broker.
- Stage instrumentation confirmed that six PubMed calls overlap at the JiuwenSwarm tool and MCP SDK request entries under `allow`, while their broker intervals remain serial. The `ask` resume path adds latency but does not cause the common serialization.

### Measured scheduler control and performance boundary

**Product-path dispatch:** In the controlled six-PubMed-call `allow` probes, the original broker calls started one after another. With the read-only concurrency opt-in, all six began within 44 ms and the source broker then applied its own queue/concurrency limits. The batches took 12.09 s and 7.22 s respectively, but their successful-result counts differed (2/6 versus 1/6); those wall times are **not** a clean successful-workload speed comparison.

**Network-free scheduler control:** A fake JiuwenSwarm adapter submitted the same six fixed-success, MCP-like calls in one model response. Each call took 150 ms; a local two-permit limiter simulated the PubMed source concurrency ceiling. Across five repetitions per mode, every call succeeded:

| Classification | Six-call batch span, five runs | Median | Max active |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exclusive | 921.2–925.6 ms | 923.4 ms | 1 |
| Parallel-safe | 451.5–454.4 ms | 452.6 ms | 2 |

This measures about a 51% shorter batch span in ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler`, with the simulated source limit intact. It does not include the real MCP broker, model, or provider. The temporary diagnostic test was removed after running.

**Real-provider support outside ScienceDiscovery:** A separate no-model harness requested the same six public PubMed topics, including eSearch and eSummary, with at most two search jobs and at most two HTTP requests per second. In serial/parallel/parallel/serial order, the batch results were 10.031 s (6/6), 6.797 s (5/6; one HTTP 429), 6.344 s (6/6), and 11.359 s (6/6). The fully successful parallel block was quicker than either fully successful serial block. This supports the scheduling direction but is **not** a product E2E before/after or evidence of a success-rate improvement. [Methods and per-run data](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/262#issuecomment-6119154713).

**Whole-run boundary:** In the earlier DA-13-3 trace, 49 literature MCP calls occupied 189.6 s across ten contiguous batches. An optimistic two-concurrent-per-source schedule estimates 89.2 s, or about **100.4 s potential saving**; that remains a scheduling estimate, not a measured whole-run improvement. The 962.5 s E2E also includes different research work and model turns. A stable-provider, same-workload MCP integration benchmark is still needed before claiming an end-to-end speedup.

### Suggested acceptance test

Classify only known read-only MCP operations as parallel-safe; keep opaque/mutating tools exclusive. Use six independent read-only MCP calls emitted in one model turn under both `allow` and `ask`. Assert broker execution intervals overlap while respecting per-source concurrency/rate limits. Also cover mixed allow/deny decisions, preapproved calls, and correct replay after interruption.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Observed in local ScienceDiscovery E2E checkouts on 2026-10-09 (Windows host + WSL Linux runtime, x86_64).
- ScienceDiscovery API/adapter with installed JiuwenSwarm/OpenJiuwen runtime; public PubMed and Europe PMC MCP tools.
- PubMed source governance allowed up to two concurrent requests and three requests per second; broker reported `queueWaitMs: 0` for the observed calls.
- The model provider is not needed for reproduction: a deterministic model stub that emits one batch of six independent MCP `tool_calls` would isolate this behavior.
- No private API key or raw trace is attached.

### Additional Information

Related: #230 documents a separate CAS commit-validation bottleneck. The MCP serialization here remains observable with that optimization applied and also under `allow`. The 100.4 s figure above remains a bounded estimate; the new scheduler and provider controls do not replace a same-workload MCP integration benchmark.

### Version Information

Observed on the 2026-10-09 ScienceDiscovery experimental E2E checkout based on commit `4ece4d3` plus the local CAS commit-validation experiment discussed in #230. The 2026-10-12 controlled probe used a separate isolated checkout based on `4cf846f`; installed runtime metadata reported `openjiuwen 0.1.17` and editable `workswarm 0.2.5b1`. This report identifies the ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` policy in the tested checkout; it does not claim that every MCP operation is safe to run concurrently.
