items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
Session-enabled MCP sources could look enabled while the agent silently received no tools. This PR now covers both connector-picker readiness and run/conversation behavior on current main: users see catalog errors and omitted tools, while the agent decides whether an omission is nonblocking or needs a repair-card wait and governed recovery in the same run.

Related to #325. All accepted reproducible behavior is implemented on this branch; current-head CI and independent final review remain pending. This PR no longer depends on unmerged #359 for UI functionality. The original private 0.2.0 deployment cause remains unknown and is not claimed diagnosed. The [agent-importance product decision](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/358#issuecomment-6230215663) remains unchanged.

## Behavior

- The picker distinguishes unavailable from degraded sources, shows catalog errors and omitted tool IDs, and displays unknown readiness if discovery/status retrieval has not succeeded. Healthy, unselected and Web sources have no warning. Plugin-disabled sources remain excluded.
- Effective Session selections include sources mounted by the selected Specialist. These are checked, labelled and cannot be independently deselected while the Specialist mounts them. Subagent-specific source failures retain agent-labelled run diagnostics.
- Opening the picker checks current status. Reload MCP catalog retries discovery through the existing API; settings changes and terminal runs refresh status too. Failed reads are visible and do not preserve a ready claim; older reads cannot overwrite newer applied updates. Reload does not change server configuration or grant permissions.
- Healthy tools retain native deferred discovery/promotion and JiuwenSwarm immediate exposure. Unhealthy selections do not unconditionally fail setup. `mcp_readiness` records nonblocking decisions or waits on the conversation repair card for important sources. Rechecks verify repairs; cancelled/failed recovery is not success.
- `mcp_recovered_call` discovers formerly omitted tools within the original affected source selection and normal broker permissions; JiuwenSwarm requests approval. Main's separate direct-execution consent/submission and no-replay rules are preserved.

The localized catalog-status presentation adapts @yuanzhou75's [PR #359](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/359), reviewed at `876dfb2a`. This branch adds the omitted-tool, effective Specialist selection, reload/update/error handling and acceptance coverage. No changes were made to that contributor's PR or branch.

## Validation

Final candidate `f73fa37f4c0ffd8ebe8c38e871b78534a031b63c` includes implementation `c66c628b` and a clean merge of current main `83dc3fdb`.

All heavy local checks used `timeout --kill-after=15s 300s`, the shared repository test lock, a 768 MiB Node heap, existing dependencies and one test worker:

| Focused check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| ConnectorPicker, MCP readiness hook, settings-loads tests | 21 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| MCP workspace tests | 16 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Native readiness/recovery, prompt, deferred-promotion tests | 5 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| JiuwenSwarm MCP readiness/approval and deferred-tool exposure tests | 2 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Web and MCP package TypeScript | Passed |
| Architecture | Passed, 283 package source files |
| Journey metadata | 63 specs, 0 errors, 11 existing legacy warnings |
| Markdown lint and local links | Passed, 126 Markdown files |
| Git diff checks | Passed |

44 selected unit tests passed. Runtime configs map MCP/workspace packages to current source, avoiding stale compiled code without builds. Early JSX runtime failures and a checkbox assertion counting warning text were corrected before the final run. `pnpm docs:check` attempted automatic dependency reconciliation and aborted for no TTY; both existing underlying documentation tools were then run directly and passed without installing dependencies. An extra UI-test typing probe was blocked by absent renderer declarations/React test globals and existing settings-loads test typing errors; product web/MCP typing passed. A new fixture typing issue discovered by that probe was corrected.

Full local UT/ST/E2E, workspace builds and stack provisioning were not run under the operator's host recovery bounds. Local dependencies were not reinstalled after main's dependency updates, so dependency integration remains a remote-CI responsibility. No paid tests.

## E2E user journeys

**Current candidate: locally BLOCKED/unexecuted; ordinary remote CI pending.** Zero browser/API/CLI/stack journeys executed locally. Focused tests are not E2E passes.

`journey-custom-mcp` now verifies: select a Session source and invoke it; select a Specialist mounting a second source and verify checked/inherited status; invoke that effective source; disable it and reload the picker to see unavailable status while the healthy source has no warning; continue a nonblocking run visibly; block an important run on a repair card; repair and invoke the recovered tool in that same run; reload and verify the warning disappears.

Historical [run 39050355602](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39050355602) completed successfully for previous PR head `7ffd16e3`. Its standard-config artifact records 21 planned/executed/passed, 0 failed/skipped on JiuwenSwarm (tested merge SHA `a0e948c1`), including the prior custom-MCP invocation/nonblocking/repair journey. That evidence does **not** validate this candidate's new picker/Specialist assertions.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: enabled-but-unusable MCP tools are visible in the picker and conversation; important missing sources can recover under normal governance. No configuration migration. No merge/enqueue/auto-merge requested. Independent main-agent final review remains required.

items.body:
When sandbox retrieval is blocked, a failed script currently has no way to request scoped egress in the conversation. This implements the accepted option 2 for #324: the default `none` socket isolation stays intact, while explicit host declarations and observed allowlist denials use the existing permission cards.

Fixes #324

## Behavior and scope

- `request_sandbox_network(hosts, purpose, runner_id?)` returns a decision and a one-use token for a **new** `run_shell(network_authorization_id=...)` call. Approval never executes or replays code. Always Allow still requires the explicit host declaration and grants only that scope.
- Tokens and matching grants bind the exact hosts to the Session, Agent run and Runner. They cannot pass to children, unrelated targets or later runs; revoked matching grants invalidate unused tokens. A derived execution epoch leaves global settings and the shared Session epoch unchanged.
- Each network-enabled Shell execution owns its gateway, so a missing-domain denial returns the correct hosts and opens the card. Managed executions remain failed on observed policy denials even when a script catches the HTTP error. Recorded files/outcomes survive consent failure; the returned instructions require reconciliation before retry.
- Deny/cancel/expiry stays offline and reports required retrieval as incomplete. Opaque scripts in `none` cannot promise automatic host discovery; that limitation and the Skill declaration contract are documented in both languages. MCP readiness, direct execution consent, private-address filtering and baseline socket policy are preserved.

## Before-fix confirmation

Confirmed on unfixed upstream main `83dc3fdb9964306ff18f962a5ac13a7b699ffacc` using an archived source snapshot with all workspace imports mapped to baseline source, actual `run_shell`/Runner execution and the real gateway/store boundaries:

- Default policy: `none`, no allowed domains. Python socket retrieval fails with `Temporary failure in name resolution`; the tool catalog lacks a network-request tool, and requesting the new action is rejected as `Unsupported permission action`.
- Allowlist `[example.org]`: a PubMed HTTPS request receives gateway 403 before DNS (instrumented DNS count **0**). Actual permission requests: **0**; result has no structured denied-host signal.

This proves the missing accepted capability. It is a bounded runtime boundary probe, not a claim of full browser reproduction or a nondeterministic model fallback.

## Validation

At `60c8d92395e7e69d91e347befee783ba846833f7`:

- Focused API/Runner/governance regression set: **83 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Permission-card rendering tests: **8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- API/Runner builds and API, Runner, Web and test-source typechecks passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: **planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4**, no failures/skips. E2E metadata: 0 errors (11 existing legacy warnings).
- Full local UT/ST/browser layers were not run under the bounded shared-host assignment. They are pending ordinary L2 after MAIN preliminary review; Draft CI only runs policy/L1. No paid suites were run.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS — production API/Runner CLI journey**, native backend, local scripted model and local HTTP target, tested clean commit `60c8d92395e7e69d91e347befee783ba846833f7`:

`node test/api/sandbox-network-consent-journey.mjs` — **6 passed steps / 0 failed / 0 blocked / 0 skipped** (24 local model requests). Covers default offline policy; deny; allow once; allow matching; Always Allow; and live allowlist-denial recovery. The local target receives zero requests before approval and exactly one after a safe new call. The first command's file side effect occurs once; the denied execution stays failed and the new retrieval succeeds. Global settings remain unchanged. The isolated local-target scenario explicitly enables the existing private-address setting; no public upstream is contacted.

Browser approval/denial journeys were added with numbered reports and local-only fixtures; **not executed locally**, pending mocked browser CI. Cross-run/Agent/Runner isolation, revocation, cancellation and no blind replay have focused regression coverage. Browser/model orchestration is not inferred from rendering tests.

Two initial API driver attempts failed due fixture assumptions (tool-result formatting, then an overlong Unix socket data path). The driver was corrected without weakening assertions; the final production journey passes.

## Discussion dispositions and attribution

The explicit owner decisions [in-chat consent](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/324#issuecomment-6219491737) and [option 2](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/324#issuecomment-6231394160) are adopted. A pre-consent bridge/socket relaxation is rejected per that decision. The bot's proposed permission action, attributed denials and scoped epoch are adopted, using execution-local derived epochs rather than broadening a shared Session epoch.

Reviewed yuanzhou75's #360 design/diff and all review threads/replies as reference; no code was copied. Its banner is deferred as optional assistance and is not a dependency. The review's scope-isolation and avoid-repeated-unrelated-prompts principles are adopted through exact run/Agent/Runner/host resources; there is no keyword-based send gate. Its App-gate-specific tests and `Fixes` wording belong to that contributor PR, which this change does not modify. The CRLF finding is avoided: changed files retain LF, and `App.tsx` is untouched.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: blocked sandbox retrieval can request exact hosts through conversation consent and continue deliberately after approval.
Compatibility and migration: no configuration migration; default offline isolation and durable global settings remain unchanged.

Draft pending MAIN independent preliminary review and L2 validation. Do not merge or enable auto-merge as part of this handoff.

items.body:
Fixes #29

Most of this issue is already on `main`. `scripts/start-stack.sh` collects every missing host tool before it exits, prints what is missing with a concrete remedy for node, pnpm, python3, uv and curl, and the Node gate reports the version it found. Two gaps remained, both on the source-mode path:

1. **The report's documentation link was dead.** Its footer pointed to `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes`, which no longer exists. The README requirements row it also points to did not list curl or Bubblewrap.
2. **Nothing told a source-mode user how to get bubblewrap or sandbox-exec.** Startup deliberately stopped checking for them; the Runner probes for them itself. When the executable is missing, the Runner's readiness report carried only the raw `spawn bwrap ENOENT`. It wrote the problem only to its log file, so the terminal said nothing. The Settings "Execution readiness" card showed `spawn bwrap ENOENT` with no remedy.

## Runner: say how to install a missing sandbox executable

- `missingSandboxExecutableMessage` in `@sciencediscovery/sandbox-capability` returns three lines:
  - **Bubblewrap:** the package is named bubblewrap and provides the bwrap executable. It gives the apt and dnf commands and links `deployment.md#linux-reports-missing-bwrap`.
  - **sandbox-exec:** it ships with macOS and is not installed separately, so a missing one means a parent sandbox or a wrong `SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH`. It links `#macos-reports-seatbelt-is-unavailable`.
- `RunnerReadiness` uses this message as `detail` when the probe cannot spawn the executable (`ENOENT`/`EACCES`). Other probe outcomes keep their current detail.
- At startup, the Runner also prints this message to the terminal that started it, so `start-stack.sh` users see it next to the rest of the startup output. The capability report and the Settings card show the same text.
- Startup still does not block on a missing sandbox; the Runner reports it instead. The `start-stack.sh` comment now says so explicitly.

## start-stack: link the current guide

- The footer now points to `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md#local-source-mode-linux--macos`. That section lists Node.js, pnpm, python3, uv, Git, curl and the sandbox per platform.
- The README "Local source mode" requirements row (English and Chinese) adds curl and Bubblewrap on Linux, so both printed links cover every dependency the report can name.
- The same stale `#local-mode-host-processes` anchor is replaced in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `services/adapter/README.md`, and an old `how-to` path in a `package-binary-release.sh` comment.

The issue's open question asked whether commands should be inline or behind a doc link. This keeps the shape already on `main`: one remedy inline and one shared link, and each entry stays at three lines or fewer.

## Validation

Tested commit: `cb3853f5`, which is this PR's head.

- Runner unit tests (`services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts`): 3 passed, including the new case. It asserts both the bubblewrap and the sandbox-exec text and the three-line limit.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): PASS, 3,874 planned, 3,874 executed, 3,874 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): PASS, 3 planned, 3 passed.
- Mocked E2E layer (`pnpm ci:e2e`): PASS, 75 planned, 75 executed, 75 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This is the browser subset; this PR's own user journey is below.
- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 126 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 126 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS.** Tested commit: `cb3853f5`. The new driver is `test/api/source-start-dependency-journey.mjs` (run with `node test/api/source-start-dependency-journey.mjs` after `pnpm build`). It goes through the real `scripts/start-stack.sh`, the built Runner and the control API on loopback. It needs no model and no network.

| # | Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `start-stack.sh --mode local` on a host with none of node, pnpm, python3, uv, curl | One report listing all five, each with a remedy line, then exit before anything starts | PASS: exit 1; `5 host dependency problem(s)`; every entry has an indented remedy; 21 lines in total |
| 2 | Same, with only Node v20.11.0 installed | The version found and how to upgrade | PASS: `Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.` then `Upgrade it, …` |
| 3 | Follow the printed links | Each `path#anchor` matches a heading that covers those dependencies | PASS: `README.md#requirements` and `deployment.md#local-source-mode-linux--macos` resolve; the README row and the guide section name every dependency; the Runner's two anchors resolve too |
| 4 | Tools present, no `bwrap` on PATH, start the Runner as `start-stack.sh` does | The terminal names the package, the binary and the install command | PASS: three lines on stderr (shown below); `/execution-capability` reports `dependency-unavailable` with the same text |
| 5 | The readiness the Web UI reads (`/api/runners/local/execution-capability`) | The same remedy reaches the Settings card | PASS: `connected: true`, `ready: false`, the detail carries the remedy and the anchor |

Totals: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped.

Terminal output of the Runner in scenario 4:

```text
bubblewrap is not available: "bwrap" could not be started (spawn bwrap ENOENT).
Install the bubblewrap package, which provides the bwrap executable: sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap (Debian/Ubuntu) or sudo dnf install -y bubblewrap (Fedora/RHEL/openEuler). Then recheck the Runner.
Details: docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md#linux-reports-missing-bwrap
```

The Settings → Local Runner "Execution readiness" card on the same kind of stack, in a headless browser. Before this change, the card's message line read only `spawn bwrap ENOENT`:

![Execution readiness card naming the bubblewrap package, the bwrap executable, the install commands and the troubleshooting section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d190210-514b-4f56-8afb-f03c23ab5340)

The macOS `sandbox-exec` path could not run on this Linux host. Its message is covered by the unit test, which probes a missing `sandbox-exec` path on Linux and gets the same spawn failure.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`
User impact: A source-mode start that fails on host tools now links a guide section that exists. A host without bubblewrap, or with a broken sandbox-exec, is told in the terminal and in Settings what to install or check.
Compatibility and migration: none. The readiness `reason` values are unchanged; only the human-readable `detail` of the missing-executable case changes.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Fixes #30

Neither README mentions `ScienceDiscovery run`, so a researcher who wants to script or batch runs has no way to learn the command-line client exists. The deployment guides show only `serve`, and the CLI reference never names the flag a non-interactive run needs. This PR adds a short command-line section to both READMEs, a command list to both deployment guides, and names `--auto-approve` in the CLI reference.

## README: command line (English and Chinese)

- A new **Command line** section after the capability table shows three runnable commands: a terminal run, a piped run filtered with `jq`, and an answer written to a file. One paragraph states the TTY versus pipe difference, that a non-interactive run must pass `--auto-approve`, and what that option allows: it approves the session's tool actions, except direct host execution after a sandbox failure, which always needs explicit consent.
- The examples differ from the issue's sketch on purpose. On current `main`, `run "…" > answer.md` does not produce a clean file: a redirected stdout is not a TTY, so `run` defaults to JSONL and refuses to start without `--auto-approve`, which leaves one JSON error line in the file and exits 1 (scenario 6 below). The file example therefore uses `--auto-approve --output text`.
- The capability table gets a **Scripted and batch runs** row, and the Documentation table's Reference row links the CLI reference.
- Commands, defaults and behaviour come from `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` and `services/launcher/src/run.ts` at `cf6c71c2`.

## Deployment guides and CLI reference

- The guide this issue names, `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md`, now lives at `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md`. Both language versions now list `serve`, `run`, `extract`, `version` and `help` in matching tables, with a pointer to the CLI reference and the source-mode entry point.
- The CLI reference exists in both languages, so the README links to it. It now says `--auto-approve` (or `--approval always_allow`) instead of "the appropriate automatic-approval option", and shows the text-to-file example.

## Relationship with #219, #27 and #318

#219 removed an earlier README command-line section to simplify the homepage. This issue's acceptance criteria ask for the CLI in both READMEs, so it returns as one short section (three commands, one paragraph) that leaves the option list to the CLI reference. #27 (README security warning) is a separate pull request; the two change different lines and `git merge-tree` merges them cleanly in either order. They also merge cleanly with open #318.

## Validation

- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 126 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 126 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- The added docs-site links (CLI reference, English and Chinese) return HTTP 200.
- The UT, ST and mocked E2E layers were not run locally. This diff changes only Markdown (READMEs, deployment guides, CLI reference), with no code, test or build input; this PR's CI runs them.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS.** This was a CLI journey over the commands the README documents. Tested code: `cf6c71c2`; this PR's head differs from it only in Markdown. The journey ran when the head was `809c6fcf`. The later commit `3fe05546` only rewords two sentences after review and leaves the commands unchanged. It ran against an isolated local stack built from source, with the sandbox runner and control API on loopback, the native agent loop, and scientific environments off. A real model served it (`deepseek-flash` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The client was `node services/launcher/dist/main.js run`, the source-mode equivalent of `./ScienceDiscovery run`. It ran from the directory that holds `./.sciencediscovery-data`, with `--port` matching `serve`, as the README says.

| # | Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `help` | Lists the five commands in the new deployment tables | PASS: 5 of 5 |
| 2 | Terminal example, stdout on a pseudo-terminal | Text mode, interactive, answer on stdout, progress on stderr | PASS: exit 0, `interactive=true approval=ask_for_dangerous`, answer on the terminal, `[run]` lines only on stderr |
| 3 | Pipe example: `--auto-approve` piped through the README's `jq` filter | JSONL only; the filter prints the final answer | PASS: exit 0, 545 lines, 0 non-JSON lines, `result.status=completed`, 3,033-byte answer |
| 4 | `--auto-approve --output text "…" > answer.md` | The file holds only the answer | PASS: exit 0, 2,060-byte answer, 0 status or JSON lines in the file, `[run] completed` on stderr |
| 5 | Pipe without `--auto-approve` | Refused with a JSON error | PASS: exit 1, `{"type":"error",…,"code":"NON_INTERACTIVE_NO_AUTO_APPROVE"}` |
| 6 | The issue's `run "…" > answer.md` without flags | Shows why the README differs | Exit 1; the file holds the JSON refusal, not an answer |

Totals: 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped.

How long a run takes depends on what the agent decides to do. The same pipe example finished in 8 s on one run and in 478 s on another, where the agent chose to research first. The README promises no timing. In an earlier attempt at scenario 2, the agent asked to write a file. The permission menu appeared in the terminal, and answering `1` let the run complete.

One defect showed up that this PR does not change. When an interactive run waits about five minutes at a permission prompt, the client prints `[run] failed: terminated` and stays at `Choose [1-3]:`, while the run is still `blocked` on the server. The likely cause is that the run event stream sends nothing while blocked, so the client's idle body timeout closes it.

## Release

Release category: `release:docs`
User impact: Readers of either README learn that the command-line client exists, how to script it, and why a non-interactive run needs `--auto-approve`. Both deployment guides now list every launcher command.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #27

The README rework this issue asks for has landed on `main`, except for one acceptance item: "The security warning is still present and unsoftened". Commit 39cf7a16 (in #223) removed the `[!WARNING]` block from both READMEs without a replacement. What remains is a note to keep the sign-in URL private, and that note does not say the service is single-user, has no TLS, or where the sandbox boundary is. This PR restores the warning in both languages.

## The warning

- It sits at the end of **Requirements**, below the getting-started path (Installation, Configure a model, First task) and not above the pitch, as the issue proposes. That is also where it was before its removal.
- The original text is kept word for word: not a multi-user production service; adapter and API on loopback by default; one bearer token; no TLS termination; exposing them elsewhere is an explicit choice for a trusted network; Python, R and shell run in a fail-closed sandbox (Bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt in macOS source mode); the control plane runs outside it.
- Two boundaries the old text did not cover are added, so a reader is not told less than the docs say:
  - STDIO MCP servers you configure run on the API host, outside the session sandbox (`docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-custom-mcp.md`).
  - Host execution after a sandbox failure is a recovery step with its own explicit approval and no sandbox isolation (`docs/en/developer-docs/sandbox-execution.md`).
- It ends with a link to the Sandbox execution page on the docs site.

The facts were checked against `cf6c71c2`. `SCIENCE_AGENT_HOST` defaults to `127.0.0.1` in the API (`services/api/src/bootstrap/config.ts`), the adapter (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/config.py`) and the launcher (`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts`). Compose publishes on `127.0.0.1` unless `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST` is set. A stack started from this commit with default settings listened on `127.0.0.1` only.

## Other acceptance items at `cf6c71c2`

These are already met on `main` and are unchanged here:

- The first screen has the pitch, a product GIF, and Download, Quick start and Documentation links.
- Every capability row links to a page.
- Installation names the Releases page and the asset per architecture.
- Both READMEs have the same structure, and the Chinese introduction no longer repeats the hero line.
- "300+ Skills" is gone; the README now says "cross-domain skill library", with a link to the Skills page.

## Relationship with #223, #377 and #318

#223 gave no reason for dropping the warning. If maintainers prefer it to live only in the deployment docs, the alternative is to change this acceptance item instead of merging this PR. #377 (the README command-line section for #30) is a separate pull request; the two change different lines and `git merge-tree` merges them cleanly in either order. This PR also merges cleanly with open #318.

## Validation

- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 126 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 126 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- The added docs-site links (Sandbox execution, English and Chinese) return HTTP 200.
- The UT, ST and mocked E2E layers were not run locally. The diff adds six lines of Markdown to the two READMEs; this PR's CI runs them.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. The change is static README text. It changes no product path that a browser, API, CLI or local-stack journey could exercise. The one behavioural claim it restates, loopback binding by default, was checked on a locally started stack from `cf6c71c2`, as noted above.

## Release

Release category: `release:docs`
User impact: Both READMEs again warn that the service is single-user, unencrypted and loopback-bound by default, and say what runs outside the sandbox.
Compatibility and migration: none.

items.body:
Contributors had no documented step for taking ownership of an existing issue or keeping its plan and progress on the issue. Document self-assignment when implementation starts, followed by English plan and progress comments, while preserving other contributors' ownership and text.

## Changes

- Restore the general **edit only items you created** rule. The only exception is adding yourself as an assignee when starting to implement an issue; comments remain allowed.
- Add **Working on an issue** before CONTRIBUTING's pull-request section. Skip assignment only when **you are already an assignee**. When others are assigned, add yourself and say in a comment that you are also working on it.
- Extend the GitHub skill with `gh issue edit <n> --repo openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery --add-assignee @me`, a fallback using the current `gh` login, and a readback check that the assignees include that login. Keep existing assignees.
- Post an English plan describing the intended change and completion criteria even if self-assignment does not persist. If readback does not include your login, do not retry or report the issue as assigned: say you are working on it and ask a maintainer to assign you in the plan comment. The `"$login"` fallback only covers `@me` being unavailable, not missing assignment permissions. Keep progress on the issue and leave other people's titles, bodies and comments unchanged.
- Exclude reading, a brief answer and issue creation alone from self-assignment. Link the PR skill to the same workflow rather than duplicating commands.

Only CONTRIBUTING and the two GitHub/PR skills change. There are no workflow, CI, CODEOWNERS or product changes.

## Validation

CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

Automatically generated Session titles could expose inline reasoning and were cut off at 24 characters even when that left an incomplete English phrase. This change generates complete summaries, filters reasoning, and separates stored titles from sidebar overflow styling.

## Changes

- Summarize the first message's core topic or intent in the user's language. Target 8–16 characters for CJK (maximum 24, including spaces and Latin names); target 3–6 words for other languages (maximum 8 whitespace-separated words and 80 Unicode characters).
- Regenerate once from the original message when the model exceeds the budget, returns an ellipsis, or reports truncated visible output. Preserve the complete accepted phrase instead of slicing it. Aggregate provider usage across successful responses.
- Use a neutral provisional `Session MM-DD HH:mm` title for long messages. Failed, empty, or still-invalid refinement retains that safe title; manual renames remain protected.
- Strip nested, unclosed and ordinary `<think>` blocks. Never use separate provider reasoning as the title.
- Keep sidebar ellipses in CSS; the existing full-title tooltip remains available. Existing stored titles and manual titles are not migrated.

## Policy and comparison evidence

The [title policy and acceptance examples](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346/docs/en/developer-docs/session-titles.md) document long Chinese/English cases and distinguish public evidence from assumptions. Open WebUI's public prompt and sidebar source show short topic summaries and CSS overflow; LibreChat documents a language-aware short-title prompt. Claude's help documents renaming but does not disclose its naming algorithm. The language budgets and bounded regeneration above are our own policy, not claimed competitor internals.

## Validation

Remote implementation: 324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346. Its Git tree b8ee654a0d702a192673a8f1b7a26a7afb9d832b is verified identical to locally validated commit 1624420d544008eebc6f4c2cb856a7be85e6ff69. GitHub Git Data API was used because the Git transport was unreachable.

- Title unit suite: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Cases include long Chinese/English outputs, regeneration, language-budget boundaries, incomplete output, nested reasoning, safe rejection and aggregated usage.
- Workspace build: **32 package/service projects completed**.
- API/schema type checks and `tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Documentation: **127 files linted, 0 issues; 126 files checked for links**.
- E2E metadata: **62 spec files, 0 errors** (11 existing legacy warnings).
- Pinned Playwright discovery: **1 new journey discovered**.
- Local full UT/ST/mocked E2E layers could not complete on the available Windows host: Bash/process-spawning limitations prevent the Linux-oriented runners from reaching their cases. WSL provisioning was also unsuccessful. These are coverage limitations, not passing results. No real-model quality evaluation was run.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED locally** — `test/journey-session-titles.spec.ts` uses a journey-owned loopback model and covers long Chinese and English first messages → oversized model output → shorter complete title → persisted title after reload → sidebar CSS and full-title tooltip. A third scenario covers reasoning-only output retaining a safe default. The stub is explicitly enabled only for this journey.

The added journey has been discovered and its metadata checked, but has not yet been executed successfully. The updated GitHub Actions run must establish the Linux full-layer results; no previous-tip CI result is presented as validation of this update.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (existing label retained).

User impact: Complete automatic titles without reasoning content or stored truncation ellipses. An oversized result may require one additional naming request.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration or API shape change; existing titles are unchanged.

Closes #314

Run all 50 public BiomniBench-DA tasks as an L5 baseline candidate, and keep large scientific workspaces, dependency installation, evaluation accounting and serial execution from blocking the rest of the suite. The private upstream tasks remain outside this PR's scope. Related to #283 (L5 only).

## Public-50 coverage and baseline contract

- Pin the public dataset to `e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235`; verify input paths, sizes and checksums; keep rubrics and reference answers outside the agent workspace.
- Preserve each task's instruction verbatim and append the requested science-research-team/multiple-subagent supplement. Retain the complete submitted prompt. This requests the workflow without claiming the skill or subagents actually ran.
- Keep the existing default AMD64 release selection and add explicit ARM64 execution with `--target-arch arm64`. Verify measured architecture against the frozen identity; never remove the check or silently duplicate the 50 tasks.
- Require scores, tool calls/rounds, generation/judge usage, sampled worker RSS and end-to-end duration. Reconcile all 50 before generating a baseline candidate. Candidate mode never approves a baseline or certifies non-regression automatically.

## Runtime stability fixes

- Reuse previously verified CAS content for unchanged workspace files only while source and CAS object identities remain unchanged. Mutations and CAS tampering invalidate reuse. This avoids repeatedly streaming multi-gigabyte inputs after every tool round.
- Respect the configured runtime PyPI mirror, preserving an explicitly supplied package index. Bound external environment commands to 180 seconds and pip network waits/retries; keep gateway stall detection enabled. No deployment-specific mirror URL is hard-coded.
- Prefer positive provider token aliases over zero placeholders, and retain the complete agent-loop usage summary instead of only the final model call.

## Failure isolation, recovery and resource protection

- Add a resumable serial suite driver derived from the frozen source plan. Finish all previously unattempted public tasks before retrying failed cases once; preserve successful results and original failure evidence.
- Disable immediate judge retries in that driver so transient evaluation failures are deferred with the other failures. Other standalone judges retain their previous retry default.
- Bound analysis inactivity and case duration. Stop only verified owned descendants, checking PID start times before signaling; an inactive analysis is recorded and deferred instead of holding the queue indefinitely.
- Check free bytes and inodes before provisioning. Remove only inactive, reconstructible environments inside the suite-owned runtime; retain dataset inputs, CAS records, artifacts and reports. Never clear shared `/tmp` or other tasks' files.
- Add evaluation-only recovery from saved `trace.md`, `answer.txt` and completed delivery evidence. Preserve successful scores separately from resource-accounting completeness. A timed-out judge request with no usage is **unknown cost**, never zero cost. Such a run still cannot pass the resource baseline; a successful re-evaluation is not mislabeled as a complete E2E rerun.

The executable entry points and operational requirements are documented in `test/benchmarks/biomnibench-da/README.md` (`suite.py` and `rescore.py`). Prepared isolated services, model/dataset access, unused ports, and adequate host resources are required.

## Validation

Published candidate: `e7ed04e20064940a132f73a5e29f5767d1783dc2`. Validation used local commit `0378b66922a544cabe921e5c4e93382f09231cc4`; the published Git tree is byte-for-byte identical (`865f1d60704b12b22ba7c9c889a9e1ee21e514e0`). GitHub API publication changed commit metadata only because Git HTTPS transport was unavailable.

- Full workspace build and TypeScript checks: passed on Windows and the isolated Linux ARM64 checkout.
- CAS/model/agent-run regressions: **42 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** on Linux ARM64.
- Environment-store regressions: **24 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Biomni gate regressions: **14 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including unknown judge usage, architecture mismatch and exactly-50 ARM64 selection with unchanged default AMD64 targeting.
- Python benchmark preparation/verification/suite/re-evaluation tests: **12 passed**; shared judge retry tests: **7 passed**.
- CI self-tests applicable on the ARM64 host: **39 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. These are not a substitute for the full AMD64 UT layer.
- E2E metadata: **62 specs, 0 errors**, with 11 existing legacy warnings. Documentation lint/link checks: passed, 126 Markdown files checked.

Full layer validation remains incomplete. The standard ST plan froze **3 identities / 0 executed / 0 passed** and failed host preflight because those identities require AMD64 while the available Linux host is ARM64. The mocked-browser E2E entry was blocked by the missing pinned Playwright installation in the new isolated checkout. The full UT entry reached isolated JiuwenSwarm/adapter provisioning but has not produced a complete layer result. The Windows L1 entry also failed to spawn `pnpm` from the Node coordinator. These are explicit validation gaps, not passing layers; this PR remains draft for CI/maintainer review.

## Real E2E evidence and limitations

The ongoing paid public-50 run remains pinned to the earlier derived candidate `51fee820a07a023662e1f4dae05ed9b538e57928`; it was deliberately not switched while running. At the recorded checkpoint, **21 distinct cases had finished: 19 passed, 2 required deferred handling**, with the remaining cases still pending/in progress. These results are **not** validation of the new candidate above and do not establish a complete baseline.

On an earlier diagnostic candidate, `da-1-3` completed the public API/local-stack journey and original-rubric adapter evaluation: **92/100**, approximately **23.17 minutes**, **3.78 GiB** sampled worker RSS, **27 tool calls / 25 rounds**. Generation usage required a separate audit of immutable model records; the raw diagnostic metrics were retained, and the usage fix is included here. `da-14-1` later produced a valid **90/100** independent re-evaluation, but missing usage for a timed-out judge attempt remains an accounting failure. No all-50 pass, approved baseline, leaderboard equivalence, or non-regression certification is claimed.

The journey submits via the public API and checks persisted evidence/artifacts. Browser screenshots do not certify that API-submitted conversations were displayed in the UI. Scores use the repository's OpenAI-compatible rubric adapter, not the upstream Gemini verifier. RSS samples can miss short peaks and double-count shared pages, and exclude remote model memory and the later judge phase. End-to-end duration excludes input preparation and judging.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`.

User impact: large-input scientific runs avoid redundant snapshots and unbounded installer waits; benchmark operators receive resumable failure-isolated execution and honest partial-accounting diagnostics.

Compatibility: no product API migration or automatic baseline approval. The new serial entry point is opt-in. Existing standalone judge retry defaults and AMD64 release targeting remain intact.

GitHub Actions for the published candidate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39031865378. Policy and L1 passed. UT, ST, mocked E2E and the other heavier jobs were skipped because the PR remains draft; this is not a full-layer pass.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

![Connector picker after the biomed server is turned off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dbf29ea-549c-49c7-b1b2-4aab3e220d86)

![Connector picker when enabled servers fail to connect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a977f904-fd31-4182-8cef-5656492cd825)

![The same failure text at a narrow width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/388977e4-55bc-42b8-9d6d-961c87f31353)

![A disabled MCP server remains on the settings page with its switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbe9e5a5-f828-4b17-a4e7-0198f386283e)

Long research runs hid available progress behind expanded input, generic branch summaries and full reasoning. The timeline now leads with research phases and bounded evidence while keeping complete transcripts available on expansion.

Refs #330, including the combined #327/#330 scope approved in the [product decision](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/330#issuecomment-6219849197). This PR is Ready for review after current-head CI and independent review; it does not auto-close the Issue. The `ready` label requests ordinary PR CI and is separate from Draft/Ready state and an approving review. The existing `needs-human` hold is retained for maintainer handoff: required approval/code-owner review and an authorized queue action remain outstanding. No queue entry or auto-merge is enabled.

## Changes
- Collapse tool input and reasoning by default. Promote task/search descriptions and reasoning headings; keep model identity, paths and usage secondary.
- Coalesce adjacent read/search/list calls into Exploring/Explored. Show five-line evidence previews, Running/Ran commands and returned-paper counts. Keep failures and approvals separate; successful completion clears output-derived warnings.
- Show live parallel-branch phases, source failures and bounded subagent progress. Preserve the latest meaningful phase across system-only turn/workspace bookkeeping, and use readable Running/Ran command summaries instead of execution JSON.
- Carry managed Shell log polling, MCP notifications/attempt errors and JiuwenSwarm bridge progress into the timeline. Coalesce expanded transcript refreshes to once per second; subagent snapshots are transient, throttled to 250 ms and capped at 16,384 head/tail characters, with one persisted terminal record.
- Distinguish progress from final results: expanded main/child/trajectory details separate them with `---`; trajectory identity matching and CLI text output use final results, while JSONL preserves every event.
- Consume startup-token fragments when navigation stays in the mounted page, update its API credential and remove the fragment. The bilingual onboarding journey explicitly checks invalid-token recovery without a page reload.
- Correct the compact-process journey's trajectory exit to use Return to conversation, and retry foreground-inbox Project deletion while asynchronous cancellation settles. Preserve completion, wake suppression, transcript-boundary, error and layout assertions.
- Document timeline behavior and producer boundaries in English and Chinese.

Progress reflects actual producer evidence. Counts are per search response rather than deduplicated totals. Silent producers and unmanaged Shell still report only at completion. Full main-tool transcript retention follows the approved product decision; append-only storage and expanded transfers grow with output. No aggregate retention quota or synthetic progress estimates are introduced.

## Validation
Recovery candidate: `a0eee874c91e9678778cf83c243e43dd89961125`; current upstream main was merged without conflicts and re-fetched before publication. Commands were serialized under the shared resource lock with 300-second timeouts and a 1536 MiB Node heap.

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web exec tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/LocalAccessToken.test.tsx tests/Orchestration.test.tsx tests/RunTimeline.test.tsx tests/SubagentConversation.test.tsx`: **80 passed, 0 failed/skipped**. Covers same-document invalid/valid token replacement, listener cleanup, phase retention, readable Shell summaries, and existing timeline/transcript behavior. The new Shell regression reproduced the defect before its fix (**16 passed, 1 failed**).

items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

items.body:
## Summary

**Draft — do not merge until the full UT/ST/browser-E2E gates and remaining integration acceptance checks below are completed.** The implementation is available for review; targeted validation passed, but full local validation is incomplete.

Extract Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and expose its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools. This is the service-extraction work for #101 (part of #84), establishing a separate lifecycle and state boundary before the evolve migration in #102.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`. The candidate is `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e` (one commit; 45 changed files, including detected moves).

## 1. Independent service and state ownership

- Move `idea_tree_service`, `research_service`, the research engine, tree models, prompts and templates from evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree/src/sciencediscovery_idea_tree`.
- Remove both router registrations from the evolve server. The new package has no imports from evolve; the existing research algorithm is preserved rather than rewritten as part of the extraction.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI entry point, health endpoint, locked dependencies, shutdown cleanup and service-only authentication. Standalone startup fails closed without `SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.
- Use a dedicated state root (`SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_DATA_DIR`, defaulting under the shared data root's `idea-tree` directory), atomic JSON persistence and independently persisted research settings.
- Copy legacy tree/research records on first startup without deleting originals. A migration marker prevents re-importing stale legacy data; conflicting destination records fail startup instead of overwriting data. Import the old API catalog's settings once, then keep settings authoritative in the service.
- Serve persisted skill references so skill deletion-impact checks include autonomous research as well as historical trees and chat-run references.

## 2. Service-owned MCP tools and capability isolation

The service publishes four tool contracts:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_idea_research` | Start autonomous research with an objective and prepared evidence/materials |
| `get_idea_research` | Query the current session's research and findings |
| `control_idea_research` | Pause, continue or end research |
| `view_idea_tree` | Read a historical tree graph |

The trusted control plane provisions a five-minute capability using its service credential. The scoped MCP endpoint supports initialization, discovery, calls, ping, notifications and revocation. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from that trusted scope, not model-supplied tool arguments. Continue grants are pinned to a specific research ID. Expired scopes are rejected, active scope count is bounded, and revoking a transport scope does not terminate autonomous research. Access logging is disabled for this process to avoid logging capability URLs.

The API obtains schemas from the service and contributes them to the existing JiuwenSwarm MCP bridge/native executor. The former hard-coded create/get tool definitions in `packages/evolve` are removed. Tool discovery failure does not prevent unrelated chat tools from being used.

## 3. TypeScript client and unchanged frontend interfaces

- Replace `services/api/src/idea-tree/python-client.ts` with `IdeaTreeServiceClient` in `packages/idea-tree`. The client provides authenticated, bounded HTTP transport, dynamic tool discovery, scoped MCP research calls, settings transport and historical-tree reads.
- Route active research through the independent service rather than evolve. Preserve the research-created event, create-time chat messages and SSE forwarding.
- Keep historical compatibility types/read transport in `packages/idea-tree`; legacy mutating `tree_*` tools remain disabled.
- Preserve all six frontend paths and their existing response shapes:

| Interface | Handling after this change | Contract mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Research service command/query | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Independent research lifecycle; control plane retains chat-message creation | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | Independent service SSE, forwarded through the existing public route | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | Historical graph read from independent storage | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned settings | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |
| `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned partial update, preserving values on an empty update | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |

These are contract-case mappings, not a claim that a full baseline/candidate L1 differential run passed. The committed lifecycle golden fixture records the stable `running → paused → paused after restart → completed` projection and is asserted by the service journey; it is not a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace.

## 4. Startup, packaging and test discovery

- Provision/start the new service through `scripts/start-stack.sh` and include it in the Docker image.
- Default to loopback port `4314`; reserve `4414` for the isolated browser-test stack and include it in busy-port checks.
- Add `pnpm idea-tree:test`, relocate the existing Python tree/research tests with the service, and include the service in tagged test discovery, environment preparation and coverage roots.
- Add standalone-service documentation covering configuration, migration and the remaining control-plane boundary.

## Compatibility, migration and scope boundaries

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained startup script/Docker packaging includes the new process; custom process supervisors must launch it and provide matching service URL/token configuration.
- Run one ASGI worker: background research tasks and short-lived scopes are process-local. Research and settings are persisted; the journey verifies recovery of paused research after restart.
- The adapter still reaches these frontend routes through the existing API control plane. Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning are **not** moved into the new service by this PR.
- Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; it does not receive provider API keys. Extracting the service does not remove that callback dependency from the wider stack.
- Prepared evidence is preserved, but this PR does not implement the artifact/provenance/CAS service tracked by #98 or change its ownership.
- This PR does not claim completion of the broader JiuwenSwarm migration or the full #101 integration acceptance matrix; full public-route differential and chat/agent trace verification remain review/validation follow-ups.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, recursive workspace build |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including test TypeScript configuration |
| Independent-service Python suite | 34 passed |
| `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` + `packages/idea-tree/src/client.test.ts` under Linux | 11 passed |
| `node test/contract/run.mjs --coverage` | Mapping check passed: 151/254 repository interface rows mapped; not 151 executed tests |
| `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh` and `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh` | PASS |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` | PASS |

Full local gates were attempted in separate checkouts of the candidate and unmodified upstream baseline `5de0ff59`:

- **UT: BLOCKED / incomplete.** `pnpm ci:ut` remained in JiuwenSwarm dependency preparation, downloading/building its Python dependencies, before the shared test runner started. The candidate attempt was manually stopped after approximately ten minutes in this layer; the baseline attempt was also stopped while in the same preparation stage. Both wrappers then recorded exit code 2 (`JiuwenSwarm could not be installed`). This is an interrupted preparation attempt, not an observed product assertion failure, and it does not establish that UT would fail on a fully provisioned host. No frozen plan or planned/executed/passed test summary was generated; those counts are unavailable, not zero-pass success.
- **ST: incomplete, with one smoke passing.** Both checkouts built successfully. The first attempts failed before planning (`A revision is required`) because WSL Git could not resolve the Windows-created temporary worktree metadata. After repairing only that metadata, both retries froze two identities. The candidate's native agent-loop smoke group reports **planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1 / failed 0 / skipped 0**; the baseline emitted the same smoke's pass event. The other identity, `swarm-sdk-contract`, requires JiuwenSwarm setup, which was still preparing dependencies when the run was stopped. No complete two-identity ST summary is available. The retries reused the exact SHA's completed install/build via `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`; no test selection was removed.
- **Browser E2E: incomplete / not executed.** `pnpm ci:e2e` was invoked on both candidate and baseline; preparation reached the pinned `.e2e` dependency installation after the workspace build. The attempts were stopped during preparation. No browser plan, executed-journey count or final summary was produced. This is not a browser PASS and not evidence of a candidate-specific failure.

Remaining local verification was deliberately stopped rather than leaving background preparation jobs running. The draft status reflects these incomplete gates; a fully provisioned Linux/CI run is still required. The initial worktree metadata error was a local harness issue, not a source change; the dependency preparation attempts do not support claiming a pre-existing upstream product defect.

## E2E user journey

**PASS** — one independent-service API/CLI journey, seven numbered steps passed, zero failed/blocked/skipped. The driver launches the installed product CLI in a separate process, with an owned data directory and a local HTTP model stub; no paid model calls or external research services are used.

Command, from the repository root after installing the service:

```sh
services/idea-tree/.venv/bin/python test/api/idea-tree-service-journey.py
```

| Step | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Discover tools and save settings | Four MCP tools exposed; settings accepted by the independent process |
| 2. Start research with prepared evidence | Research enters `running`; the real engine reaches the local model callback |
| 3. Pause active research | Paused state persists; the delayed model response does not advance the paused stage |
| 4. Restart the service | Paused research and saved settings are recovered |
| 5. Read from another session | Cross-session capability cannot access the research |
| 6. Continue and consume SSE | 19 snapshots received; research completes with independently assessed candidate score 7; no model token in frames |
| 7. Check references and delete owned research | Persistent skill reference detected; owned session research removed |

This service-level journey does not substitute for the full browser stack, public API/JiuwenSwarm integration or a live-model test. Docker/release-binary execution was not locally verified.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

User impact: research is hosted in a dedicated service with explicit MCP lifecycle controls and persistent, independently owned settings/state. Existing frontend paths remain stable.

The contributor has read-only access to upstream (`push: false`, `triage: false`), so the GitHub `release:feature` label is **pending a maintainer**; it has not been applied.

items.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）
