items.body:
## Summary

When a dependency is missing, `scripts/start-stack.sh` prints one sentence naming the requirement and exits. It never says how to satisfy it or where to read more, so the first thing a new user meets is a dead end.

## Current behaviour

`scripts/start-stack.sh` (lines 212–250):

```bash
require_command() { # <command> <failure message>
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null || { echo "$2" >&2; exit 1; }
}

require_command node   "Node.js 22.19+ is required."
require_command pnpm   "pnpm 11.1.2 is required."
require_command python3 "Python 3 is required for workspace analysis."
require_command uv     "uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments."
require_command curl   "curl is required for local service startup checks."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_BWRAP_PATH:-bwrap}" "bubblewrap is required for isolated Linux execution."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH:-/usr/bin/sandbox-exec}" "macOS sandbox-exec is required for isolated execution."
```

So on a fresh machine the entire output is:

```
pnpm 11.1.2 is required.
```

and the process exits 1.

One check already does better and is worth copying — the Node version gate reports what it found:

```
Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.
```

That is the right shape; it is just missing the "and here is how to fix it" half, and the other seven checks do not even report the found version.

## Why this matters

The target audience is researchers, not Node developers. "pnpm 11.1.2 is required" assumes the reader knows what pnpm is, that it is installed through corepack or npm, and that the version is pinned deliberately. `uv` and `bubblewrap` are worse — neither is something a scientist would have encountered, and `bwrap` is not even the name printed in the error, so searching for "bubblewrap" and searching for the binary give different results.

The information exists: `README.md` has a requirements table, and `docs/*/how-to/deployment.md` has per-platform install commands. The failure message just never points there. This is the same class of stumble reported in [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) — the product is reachable but the path to it is not explained.

## Proposal

Extend `require_command` to take a remedy, and print three things on failure: what is missing, what was found (when anything was), and one concrete next step.

```
uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments; not found on PATH.
Install:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Details:  docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes
```

Specifically:

- **node / pnpm** — name the version manager the project expects (corepack, `npm i -g pnpm@11.1.2`, or whatever is canonical here) rather than leaving the reader to pick.
- **uv** — the official install line, plus the note that it is only needed for source mode.
- **bubblewrap** — the package name per distro (`apt install bubblewrap`, `dnf install bubblewrap`) and the fact that the binary is `bwrap`, since the error names one and `command -v` looks for the other.
- **sandbox-exec** — say it ships with macOS, so "missing" almost always means a restricted parent sandbox rather than something to install; `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` already explains this, and the error should link to it.
- Report the found version wherever a version gate exists, as the Node check already does.
- Collect all failures before exiting instead of stopping at the first one, so a user on a bare machine learns everything they need in one run rather than in five.

Keep each message to two or three lines — this is not a place for a wall of text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every preflight failure names the missing dependency, what was found (if anything), and a concrete install step or doc link.
- [ ] The doc link resolves to a section that actually covers that dependency.
- [ ] The bubblewrap message reconciles the package name with the `bwrap` binary name.
- [ ] A machine missing several dependencies reports them all in one run.
- [ ] The messages stay short enough to read in a terminal.

## Open question

Should the install commands live in the script, or should the script print only a doc anchor and keep the platform-specific commands in the deployment guide? Inline commands are more immediately useful; a single doc anchor is easier to keep correct.
items.title: [Feature]: Dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery ships a real command-line client — `ScienceDiscovery run` — that can drive a full agent task, stream JSONL, read from stdin, and be scripted. **The README never mentions it in either language.** A researcher who wants to batch a hundred runs from a job script has no way to learn the capability exists short of running `help`.

## What already exists

From `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` (the binary's own `help` output):

```text
Commands:
  serve                    Start the Web UI, control API and sandbox runner
  run [input] [options]    Run an agent task via a running serve (CLI client)
  extract --to <dir>       Unpack the embedded runtime payload without starting it
  version                  Print the release version and bundled runtime versions
  help                     Show this message
```

`run` takes 13 options: `--content`, `--stdin`, `--session`, `--project`, `--model`, `--skills`, `--connectors`, `--approval`, `--auto-approve`, `--review`, `--token`, `--output <jsonl|text>`, `--timeout`.

`services/launcher/src/run.ts` documents the behaviour that makes it scriptable:

- **text mode** (default on a TTY): the answer streams to stdout, status and progress to stderr — so `run "question" > answer.md` yields a clean file.
- **jsonl mode** (default when piped): every event is one JSON line on stdout, errors included, so a downstream `jq` never meets a non-JSON line.

This is a genuinely useful capability for the target audience: reproducible batch runs from a job script, a run per dataset, output piped straight into an analysis pipeline.

## The gap

1. **Neither README mentions it.** `README.md` and `README_zh.md` contain no occurrence of "CLI", "command line", "命令行", "headless", `jsonl`, or `ScienceDiscovery run`. Quick start shows only `./ScienceDiscovery serve`.

2. **The English deployment guide omits the command entirely.** The two guides disagree:

   | Guide | Commands listed |
   |---|---|
   | `docs/zh/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, **`run`**, `extract`, `version`, `help` |
   | `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, `extract`, `version`, `help` |

   The Chinese guide also carries a worked example and the mode/approval rules; the English guide has none of it. So today the CLI is documented **only in Chinese**.

3. There is no `reference/cli.md` in either language — raised separately in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).

## Proposal

Add a short **Command line** section to `README.md` and `README_zh.md`, after Quick start — four or five lines, not a manual:

````markdown
## Command line

Besides the Web UI, a running `serve` can be driven from the terminal:

```bash
./ScienceDiscovery serve &                      # start the stack
./ScienceDiscovery run "Summarize these results" > answer.md
cat prompt.txt | ./ScienceDiscovery run --stdin --auto-approve | jq .
```

`run` connects to the same control plane as the browser and reads the token
from the data directory, so no extra setup is needed when `run` and `serve`
share a `--data-dir`. On a TTY the answer goes to stdout and progress to
stderr; when piped it emits JSONL, and a non-interactive run must pass
`--auto-approve` because it cannot answer permission prompts.
See [CLI reference](docs/en/reference/cli.md) for every command and option.
````

And alongside it:

- Add `run` to the command list in `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` so the two languages match, porting the example and the text/jsonl and approval rules from the Chinese guide.
- If the README grows a feature table ([#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27)), give scripted/batch use a row of its own — it is a differentiator worth stating, not a footnote.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both READMEs introduce the CLI with at least one runnable example.
- [ ] The README states the TTY/pipe output-mode difference and the `--auto-approve` requirement for non-interactive runs, so a first scripted attempt does not fail unexplained.
- [ ] `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` lists `run` alongside `serve`, `extract`, `version`, and `help`.
- [ ] The English and Chinese command lists match.
- [ ] The README links to a CLI reference once one exists.

## Open questions

- Does the README keep a short teaser and delegate details to the deployment guide / CLI reference, or carry a slightly fuller example?
- Should the example use the binary (`./ScienceDiscovery run`) only, or also show the source-mode equivalent?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (a `reference/cli.md` and the docs site), [#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27) (README rework).
items.title: [Docs]: Introduce the command-line interface in the README

items.body:
## Summary

The README is the first and often only page a visitor reads, and right now it does not do the three jobs it should: **say clearly what this is and who it is for, summarize the core capabilities in a scannable form, and hand the reader a path into the tutorials.** I would like it reworked around those three.

## Current state

`README.md` and `README_zh.md` are 57 lines each: intro sentence → security warning → Project positioning → Features → Related documents → Requirements → Installation → Quick start → License.

Concrete problems:

1. **The pitch is one sentence, and the second thing a visitor reads is a disclaimer.** Line 3 carries the whole value proposition; lines 7–8 are a `[!WARNING]` block about loopback binding, bearer tokens, TLS termination, and sandbox boundaries. That warning is correct and should stay in the README — but placing it above everything else means a first-time reader meets the caveats before they have any idea what the product does.

2. **"Project positioning" does not describe positioning, and the two languages disagree.** The English section is an architecture paragraph ("A browser UI communicates with a Node control API. Each agent run is driven by a Python Gateway…"). The Chinese section at the same position is a **verbatim copy of the intro sentence at line 12**. So one language repeats itself and the other answers a different question entirely.

3. **The feature list is dense prose with no links and an unsourced number.** Four bullets, each a 2–3 line paragraph. None of them links to anything — not a doc, not a tutorial, not a screenshot. The claim "over 300 cross-domain Skills" appears **only in the two READMEs and nowhere else in the repository or docs**, while `skills/` ships 18. Whatever the 300 refers to, a reader cannot verify it or find out how to reach those skills.

4. **No visuals at all.** Both READMEs contain zero images (`grep -c '!\['` → 0), while `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures — `project.png`, `task.png`, `model.png`, `skill.png`, `connector.png`, `permission.png`, `memory.png`, `quotas.png`, `evidence1–4.jpg`, and more. A product whose pitch is "watch the whole research workflow and trace every deliverable" shows the reader nothing.

5. **Exactly one tutorial link, buried at line 51 of 57**, mid-paragraph, after a `curl` health check. Nothing in the Features section points at how to actually try any of those features.

6. **The Installation section is a stub.** In full: "Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide." It never says where to get an executable — which is precisely what [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) asked.

## Proposal

Restructure both READMEs to this order:

1. **Title + one-line pitch + badges.** One sentence a researcher recognizes themselves in. Keep the existing positioning sentence if it tests well; just make it the hero line, not a paragraph competing with three other paragraphs.
2. **One screenshot or short GIF** of a real session — timeline, a generated artifact, the provenance view. Reuse what is already in `docs/images/`.
3. **"What you can do with it" — a scannable feature table**, one row per capability, each row linking to the tutorial or how-to that exercises it. Sketch:

   | Capability | What it means | Try it |
   |---|---|---|
   | Literature and data connectors | One-click access to paper and data repositories | `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md`, literature tutorial |
   | Sandboxed code execution | Agents write and run Python/R/shell in a fail-closed sandbox | dataset-analysis tutorial |
   | Task decomposition and skills | Complex tasks broken down and dispatched across skills | skills tutorial |
   | Full-chain traceability | Code, environment, logs, and evidence for every deliverable | `explanation/review-provenance.md`, tracing tutorial |

   The "Try it" column is the part that matters: every claim becomes something the reader can go do. The tutorial targets come from [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26); until those pages exist, the column points at the pages that do.
4. **Get started in three steps** — download, run, first task — with a real download location, then straight into the quick-start tutorial.
5. **Then** requirements, deployment paths, the security warning, contributing, and license. Keep the warning prominent and unsoftened, just below the getting-started path rather than above the pitch.

Also: either source the "300+ Skills" claim (link to wherever that library lives) or restate it in terms a reader can check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can tell within the first screen what the product does, for whom, and what it costs them to try.
- [ ] Every feature claim links to a page that demonstrates or documents it.
- [ ] At least one screenshot or GIF of the product appears above the fold.
- [ ] The tutorial entry point is a prominent link, not a clause in a paragraph.
- [ ] "Installation" says where to obtain a binary.
- [ ] The security warning is still present and unsoftened.
- [ ] `README.md` and `README_zh.md` have the same structure and make the same claims; the Chinese "项目定位" section no longer duplicates the intro verbatim.
- [ ] The "300+ Skills" figure is sourced or restated.

## Open questions

- Is there a public download or release page the README can link to, or is distribution internal for now?
- Screenshot or animated GIF — and can one be captured from a build that is safe to publish (no tokens, no internal hostnames)?
- What does the "300+ Skills" number count?
- Should the README carry the feature table, or stay short and delegate to a docs landing page once [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) publishes one?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (docs site + content completeness), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (tutorial series), [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) (onboarding experience), [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) (finding the download).
items.title: [Docs]: Rework the README — clear pitch, summarized core features, and links into the tutorials

Revising a Markdown report can drop its Evidence chips, so the next review treats the same citations as unresolved and starts another revision loop.

## Expected

If a new version of a report still contains an `[evidenceN]` marker, and this run did not publish a replacement mapping, keep the version-scoped Evidence reference from the previous version. Do not keep a marker that the new text deleted. The first revised version should still open the Memory chips, and a quick evidence check should not report `CITATION_EVIDENCE_ALIAS_UNRESOLVED` for citations that did not change.

## Actual

After Reviewer returns `REVISE_AND_RETRY`, the lead edits the same report and declares a new artifact version without calling `declare_claim` again for the unchanged citations. The new text still shows `[evidenceN]`, but that version's `references` can be empty. The next quick check then flags every remaining marker.

`SessionStore` copies the base version's references only when `baseVersionId` is set and the caller does not pass its own `references` (`services/api/src/store.ts`). `declareWorkspaceArtifact` otherwise attaches only the references drained from this run's claim calls (`packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts`). A declaration that names the artifact and omits `base_version_id` therefore stores no references. When `base_version_id` is set, every previous reference is copied, including aliases the new text removed.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/108
items.title: [Bug]: A revised report can lose Evidence chips unless base_version_id is set

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Background

We want to automate the workflow from issue submission through code changes, review, and PR merge. This requires clear repository conventions so contributors and automation can determine whether an issue is ready for implementation, whether a change meets its acceptance criteria, and whether a PR is ready to merge.

The existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers development setup, test commands, E2E testing, and some PR requirements. Extend it with issue, commit, review, and merge conventions, supported by templates and checks that all contributors can use.

### Scope

#### 1. Issue requirements

Provide templates for feature requests, bug reports, and other supported issue types. Identify required and conditional fields:

- Background, the problem to solve, and the expected outcome.
- Functional specifications, including inputs, outputs, behavior, boundary conditions, and applicable compatibility requirements.
- Scope and explicit exclusions.
- Verifiable acceptance scenarios with preconditions, actions, and expected results. Cover success, failure, permissions, and recovery where relevant.
- Reproduction steps, environment, actual behavior, and expected behavior for bug reports.
- Dependencies, open questions, and blockers that must be resolved before implementation.

Include a complete example and define when an issue is ready for development. Clarify ambiguities that affect implementation or acceptance before work begins. Update the issue when the specification changes during implementation.

#### 2. Commit and PR requirements

Document branch, commit, and PR conventions:

- Follow the existing fork and target-branch workflow, and define naming and commit message formats.
- Link the PR to its issue and explain the reason, resulting behavior, and scope.
- Map each issue acceptance criterion to its implementation and validation result.
- Provide reproducible test commands, results, and supporting evidence. Distinguish tests that were not run, failed, were blocked, or were skipped.
- Describe compatibility impact, configuration changes, data migration, and rollback where applicable.
- Update affected documentation and follow the existing release label requirements.

#### 3. Review and merge requirements

Provide a shared review checklist and define:

- Checks for specification compliance, acceptance coverage, correctness, module boundaries, and applicable security and compatibility requirements.
- The distinction between blocking findings and suggestions, including how findings are resolved.
- Responsibilities for automated and human review, including approval authority.
- Which checks and approvals must be repeated after a PR changes.
- Conditions for entering the merge queue and completing the merge, consistent with the existing CI and `merge-gate` mechanism.

#### 4. Rule checks

Maintain a rule list that states applicability, verification method, execution stage, and failure handling for each rule. Include:

- Required issue and PR information and their linkage.
- Type checks, tests, user-perspective E2E testing, and documentation checks.
- License headers, sensitive information, temporary files, and generated files.
- Module dependency boundaries and compatibility requirements.
- Required checks, review decisions, and unresolved blockers.

Enforce rules through templates or CI where they can be checked programmatically. Provide explicit instructions for rules that require human judgment. Unavailable test prerequisites must be reported as blocked. Document the reason, approver, and follow-up for any exception.

### Deliverables

- Extend `CONTRIBUTING.md` as the common entry point, linking to separate documents where needed.
- Add issue templates, a PR template, and a review checklist.
- Provide a feature issue example and a corresponding PR acceptance report example.
- Map rules to automated checks, distinguishing existing checks, checks added in this work, and follow-up work.
- Resolve duplicated or conflicting guidance and identify where each rule is maintained.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contributors can find issue, commit, PR, review, and merge requirements from one entry point.
- [ ] The feature template requires functional specifications and verifiable acceptance scenarios; the bug template requires reproduction details.
- [ ] The PR template requires an issue link, per-criterion acceptance results, and test evidence.
- [ ] The review checklist defines blocking findings, approval responsibilities, and re-review requirements.
- [ ] Merge conditions are consistent with the existing CI, merge queue, and `merge-gate` contract.
- [ ] Important rules specify applicability, verification, and failure or exception handling.
- [ ] At least one complete issue-to-PR example is included.
- [ ] New or changed templates and automated checks are validated, and documentation checks pass.

This issue covers the guidelines, templates, and agreed checks. Implementation of the complete automation system can be tracked separately.
items.title: Complete contribution guidelines for the workflow from issues to PR merge

A JSON artifact, especially a large one, is still shown from a truncated preview, so the document looks incomplete.

## Expected

The artifact viewer shows the full JSON document, or it states the preview limit and offers the complete file. A large file should not look like part of the data is missing.

## Actual

In `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, a JSON record array uses the table preview and other JSON uses `JsonSourcePreview`. Both paths carry a `truncated` flag. The raw fallback renders `source.slice(0, 100_000)`. A large artifact therefore cannot be read in full in the viewer. The original report was that this incompleteness showed up intermittently, and was most visible on large JSON files.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Cancelling or disconnecting a sandboxed execution can leave that execution running until the script exits, when the machine is under CPU pressure. The caller already sees an abort error.

## Expected

After the client disconnects or the run is cancelled, the Runner kills the sandbox process group promptly. The execution leaves `activeExecutions` in a short time that does not grow with the payload.

## Actual

On an idle machine, aborting `time.sleep(30)` or `time.sleep(60)` cleared `activeExecutions` in about 75 ms. With the Runner and busy loops pinned to the same core, the same abort often took about 30250 ms for a 30-second sleep and about 60238 ms for a 60-second sleep. One 60-second case was still running after 120 seconds. The sandbox had not been killed; it ran to completion, and only then dropped out of `activeExecutions`.

`services/runner/src/executor.ts` registers the abort listener after `spawnSandboxProcess` resolves. `killSandboxProcess` then sends `SIGKILL` to the process group, which is the right signal once it runs. The kill does not run until the event loop observes the abort. A starved loop still lets the payload finish. The same path is what the product uses when a person cancels a long run in the interface.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/71
items.title: [Bug]: Cancelling a run under CPU pressure can leave the sandbox running until the script exits

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
A parent run that launches several `task` subagents in one turn can fail while persisting the children's results, even though the children themselves finish.

## Expected

A completed subagent handoff is stored, and the parent run stays successful. Nested fields inside the child snapshot are not treated as content-addressed references.

## Actual

The parent run ends with `Agent run failed` and the UI reports `Invalid or cross-pool reference`. The children have already finished. A later user message can receive their completion notices, but that is a new run, not a resume of the failed one.

The `task` tool returns `details: { subagent, summary }` from `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`. The native agent writes that object into a `ToolObservation` in `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts`. `ContentStore.putRecord` in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts` walks every nested object that has both `pool` and `digest`, and rejects a value that is not a complete object in the current pool. A real subagent snapshot can contain those shapes from another pool, or an incomplete reference, so the parent fails at the result boundary.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/87
items.title: [Bug]: Parallel subagent results can fail the parent run with Invalid or cross-pool reference

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
items.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable

## Summary

Enabling scientific connectors (`arxiv`, `pubmed`) on a Session persists `enabledConnectorIds`, and `/api/connectors` lists those sources, but the live agent tool set can still contain **no** `mcp__arxiv__*` / `mcp__pubmed__*` tools. Literature runs then fall back to `web_search` only. This breaks the documented contract that Session-enabled MCP sources become governed agent tools (control-plane MCP, outside the sandbox).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** local instance.
2. Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["arxiv","pubmed"]` (and typically `web`).
3. Confirm `/api/connectors` returns arXiv/PubMed manifests (`enabledByDefault: false`, `requestedCapabilities: ["mcp"]`, NCBI/arXiv `networkHosts`).
4. Run a literature workflow that activates `literature-searcher` (or ask the main agent to search PubMed/arXiv via MCP).
5. Observe run events / agent reports: **no** literature MCP tool calls; agent/subagent states that no literature-search MCP tool is present; only `web_search` (and failed `web_fetch`) are used.

Observed on session `27148ad0…`, run `dad3a25d…`.

## Expected

- If a connector id is in the Session’s effective `enabledConnectorIds` and the MCP source is **ready**, the corresponding tools (`mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>`, e.g. `mcp__pubmed__search`, `mcp__arxiv__search`) must appear in the agent/subagent tool set (native: deferred directory + promotion; JiuwenSwarm: promoted at start per docs).
- If the underlying MCP server/catalog is **unavailable** or **degraded**, enabling the connector must not look “on with tools”; the run/UI/agent should surface catalog status (or refuse the enablement path) instead of silently omitting tools while checkboxes stay enabled.

## Actual

Session JSON and connector catalog UI/API show arXiv/PubMed enabled/listed, but `createMcpWorkspaceTools` injects nothing for those sources when `McpSourceCatalog.getStatus(...).availableTools` is empty. The agent proceeds with an empty MCP tool list and no hard error tied to the enabled connectors.

## Code pointers

Injection chain (also documented in `docs/zh/developer-docs/science-connectors.md` §3):

1. **Session enablement** → `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` passes `enabledSourceIds: settingsSnapshot.enabledConnectorIds` into `createMcpWorkspaceTools` (after `filterEnabledMcpSources` for plugin master/per-connector switches).
2. **Catalog gate** → `packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` (`createMcpWorkspaceTools`): keeps only tools in `catalog.getStatus(sourceId).availableTools`. Empty `availableTools` ⇒ no tools for that source.
3. **Why `availableTools` can be empty** → `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts` (`statusFor` / `getStatus`):
   - Catalog never refreshed → status `unavailable`, `availableTools: []`, error *"MCP catalog has not been refreshed"*.
   - MCP server `biomed` missing/disabled/errored → same empty list (`transport.mcpServerId: "biomed"` in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`).
   - Remote `listTools` missing or schema-incompatible with local `mcpToolName` (e.g. `pubmed_search`, `arxiv_search`) → `degraded` / tool omitted.
4. **Startup soft-fail** → `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`: `mcpCatalog.refresh().catch(...)` only warns; API keeps running with an empty/failed catalog while `/api/connectors` still lists manifests from the registry (no status). Status lives on `/api/mcp/sources` instead.
5. **Deferred visibility** (native) → `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` marks MCP tools `deferred: true`. That only applies to tools that survived step 2; it does not explain a completely empty MCP set.

Related but separate: skill scripts under `skills/literature-searcher/scripts/*` need `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXTERNAL_URLS_PATH` / `config/external-urls.json` in the sandbox; that does **not** replace MCP injection. Skill docs say to use session MCP tools and not bundled scripts for literature search.

## Impact

- Users believe PubMed/arXiv are connected; retrieval silently degrades to web snippets.
- `literature-searcher` cannot fulfill its MCP-first contract.
- Hard to debug without checking `/api/mcp/sources` status vs Session checkboxes.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Treat “enabled but catalog unavailable/degraded” as a first-class Session/run signal (surface status next to connector toggles; emit a run warning or block start when every enabled literature source has zero `availableTools`).
- Ensure bundled `biomed` stdio MCP from `extensions_config.json` is healthy before advertising connectors as usable.
- Optionally include catalog status in `/api/connectors` so the UI cannot show “enabled” without readiness.

## Labels

bug, needs triage

## Summary

System configuration → Skills → Import offers **Folder**, but the desktop/file control only accepts a **file path**. Choosing a skill package directory is rejected. Importing a lone `SKILL.md` works, which is fine for docs-only packages and **drops** `scripts/` / `references/` / `assets/` for richer packages.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, Scenario 2 Case A (2026-10-15):

1. Skills → Import → Folder.
2. `setInputFiles` / file control on directory `/workspace/.../fixtures/csv-quality-check/` → rejected (directories not accepted).
3. Importing `/workspace/.../fixtures/csv-quality-check/SKILL.md` succeeded → Managed · r1 `csv-quality-check`.
4. That fixture had no scripts; a package with scripts would be incomplete via SKILL.md-only import.

UI also lists ZIP and Git repository (not exercised in this pass).

## Expected

- Folder import should accept a directory and preserve the full package layout, **or**
- If the browser/host cannot do directories, disable/hide Folder and steer users to ZIP / Git with clear copy.
- Do not advertise Folder if the control can only take a file.

## Priority

**Medium** for authors shipping skills with scripts/references.

## Related

Custom MCP absence is separate ([Bug] custom MCP /api/mcp/servers 404 — filed in the same pass).

## Summary

On the L5 real E2E run ([38734441039](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38734441039), commit `768688fa`, product code identical to `844947da`, judge `deepseek-flash` at temperature 0), BiomniBench-da-13-3 and BiomniBench-da-14-1 scores move much more than the other research cases. Each case was scored four times (three initial runs plus one rerun of the low attempt). All four scores count.

| Case | Scores | Mean |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| da-13-3 | 78 / 59 / 78 / 100 | 78.75 |
| da-14-1 | 83 / 100 / 100 / 93 | 94.00 |

The spread is not one cause. Some points move because a later answer actually meets a written requirement. The rest move because the same kind of answer receives different grades. This issue tracks the case and rubric changes. It does not ask for another research rerun.

The formal L5 numbers are in the test-result comment on #343: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/343#issuecomment-6207027843

## What changed across the four grades

The judge reads both the trace and the answer. Each of the eight answers was scored once. Levels below are A/B across the four runs, in order.

| Case | Criterion | Levels | Where the points go | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| da-13-3 | 3, rank significant proteins by absolute effect size | B / B / B / A | rerun +13 | The runs. The first three rank by adjusted p. The rerun lists a top set by absolute estimate for each phenotype in the trace. |
| da-13-3 | 4, biological explanation of the shared proteins | A / B / A / A | run 2 −14 | Ambiguous rubric, applied inconsistently. None of the four answers states the mechanism the A level asks for. Run 2 is the one marked B. |
| da-13-3 | 5, place the result back in the study frame | B / B / B / A | rerun +9 | The runs. Only the rerun states that the proteome tracks a treatment-driven increase in fat mass and that body composition and hormones act together, with a citation. |
| da-13-3 | 6, source reliability | A / B / A / A | run 2 −5 | Ambiguous rubric. All four answers have a reference list and some unsourced functional claims. Run 2 has the fullest citations and is the only B. |
| da-14-1 | Not the rubric's 21 endotype scores | 38, 26, 38, then 37 columns reduced to 26 | no score gap by itself | Both. The task text the agent sees does not say 21, and the rubric does not name which 21 columns. Every run still fails to narrow to that set. |
| da-14-1 | 1, load and check the score columns | B / A / A / B | run 1 and the rerun, −7 each | Ambiguous rubric. A 38-column answer is B once and A once. A 26-column answer is also A once and B once. The completeness notes are similar. |
| da-14-1 | 2, correlation matrix | B / A / A / A | run 1 −10 | Ambiguous rubric. Runs 1 and 3 both compute a full 38×38 Spearman matrix. One is marked B for not being 21×21. The other is marked A for being broader than 21×21. |

Point values used for the check: da-13-3 criteria 1–6 are A/B = 15/8, 15/7, 25/12, 27/13, 18/9, 0/−5. da-14-1 criteria 1–2 are A/B = 15/8, 20/10. Each scorecard sums to the published total.

## What this does not separate

Temperature is 0 and each request returned on the first try, but every request had a different trace and answer. That does not measure how often the judge would change its grade given the same input.

## Follow-up

- Do not rerun the research tasks to chase these scores.
- Score each of the eight existing answers several times, unchanged, and report how often the grade moves.
- Name the 21 endotype-score columns in the task text or in the rubric.
- Rewrite da-13-3 criteria 4 and 6 so an A is a checklist a second reader can mark without guessing.

Evidence is the `quality-scorecard.json`, `answer.txt`, and `trace.md` artifacts on run 38734441039 (`real-e2e-evidence-a2-research-1-r1` and `-r3` for da-13-3 attempt 2; `real-e2e-evidence-a1-research-2-r1` and `-r4` for da-14-1 attempt 1; the other two attempts are the matching `-r1` artifacts).

## Summary

Every new session defaults to **Ask for dangerous actions**, even inside a project where the user already set **Always allow** on prior sessions. There is no project- or global-level default, so demos and repeated analysis require toggling the composer control every time.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 local demos (Scenarios 1–3, 2026-10-15/16):

- New project opens an Untitled session with approval = Ask.
- User must flip the composer control to **Always allow** (`aria-pressed=true`) before tools run smoothly.
- Creating another session in the same project resets to Ask again — not inherited from the sibling session or project.

Affects projects **数据分析演示**, **自定义扩展演示**, **科学计算演示**.

## Why it hurts

For trusted local sandboxes and scripted demos, re-confirming every session adds friction and invites accidental runs still on Ask (more interrupt cards) or forgetting to tighten back later.

## Expected

- Remember last choice per project, **or**
- Offer a project/global default (Ask / Always allow) that new sessions inherit, with a clear per-session override.

## Priority

**Medium** usability — repeated friction, not a functional blocker.

## Related

Distinct from sandbox egress solicitation (#324).
items.title: Usability: approval mode resets to Ask on every new session (no project-level default)

## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session **timeline is too engineering-oriented**. Parallel tool cards, subagent workspace paths, and token/turn counters dominate the main pane, so a researcher cannot quickly see *what is happening for the research task*. Progress that does exist is buried (e.g. a sidebar tooltip like `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`) while the main area stays on a large **INPUT** dump.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, ~7 min raw screen recording):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards filled the timeline with long specialist prompts (INPUT), UUIDs / `subagents/…` paths, model name, turn counts, and token usage.
- Primary status was often just `Running` / `Tool is running…`.
- The more human-readable status (`PubMed search … · running`) appeared mainly as a **sidebar hover tooltip**, not as the main-pane headline.
- Researchers scanning the UI struggled to answer: which searcher is doing what, what failed, how many papers so far, when synthesis starts.

## Why this is a serious usability problem
This is a research workbench UX issue, not mere polish:

1. Cognitive load: engineering telemetry (paths, tokens, raw INPUT) competes with the research narrative.
2. Progress opacity: meaningful status is secondary (tooltip / deep in cards) while the main column looks like a developer console.
3. Trust: when retrieval degrades (no MCP tools, sandbox/network failures), the timeline does not make the failure mode obvious at a glance.

Related but distinct from #327 (no incremental progress at all). Here the problem is **information hierarchy / audience**: even when something is updating, the wrong details are foregrounded.

## Expected behavior
For literature / research sessions (and ideally by default for non-debug users):

1. Timeline cards should lead with a **human-readable phase** (e.g. “Searching PubMed for clinical CRISPR/SCD papers”, “Source unavailable”, “Synthesizing 5 papers”).
2. Keep subagent paths, full INPUT blobs, token/turn stats behind an expand/debug control — not the default above-the-fold view.
3. Surface parallel branches as short labeled lanes (clinical vs mechanism) rather than two giant opaque tool cards.
4. Put the same status that today only appears in the sidebar tooltip into the main timeline card header.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Default “Researcher” timeline vs optional “Developer / debug” density.
- Collapse tool INPUT by default; show a one-line summary + live status.
- Promote connector/search failures into the card status line as soon as they happen.

## Priority
**High among usability issues** for research users (serious scanability / trust problem), though not a functional crash.

## Related
- #327 — long runs only show `Tool is running…` (progress missing)
- #325 — connectors enabled but MCP tools omitted (functional bug that makes the opaque timeline worse)
- #324 — sandbox egress should ask for permission
items.title: Usability: session timeline is too engineering-heavy for researchers (tool cards, subagent paths, tokens)

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`** 与 [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta) 同属 **0.3.0 正式版前的预发布版本**：在既有 JiuwenSwarm 科研工作台能力之上，继续收敛质量与工程化交付，为正式版做候选验证。

上一版本为 `0.3.0-beta`（2026-09-30）。本版本汇总 **2026-10-01 → 2026-10-16**（Asia/Shanghai）已合并进 `main` 的变更。

> 本文是面向社区征求意见的 **Release Note 草案**，不是正式发版公告；正式 GitHub Release / tag 将另发。

## Release Note 草案

### 新功能

- **L1–L5 多级 CI 门禁**：按 PR → merge → daily → release 分层累积质量检查，Nightly/Release 真实 E2E 与 hermetic 检查并行落地（#259，相关 #280、#255、#258）。

### 主要修复

- **沙箱 / Runner 未就绪**：启动与 Runner 就绪解耦；执行仍 fail-closed；Agent 可通过 `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` 等待，并弹出重试/切换/取消恢复卡片；区分「展示等待」与「授权修复」（#275 / #265，#282）。
- **不可解析 tool call**：长科研 run 中改为扣留并恢复，不再误报为模型配置错误并整段结束主/子 Agent（#247 / #236）。
- **自定义模型设置**：任一设置接口失败时保留 provider 预设，避免 Custom provider 空表单卡死（#288 / #281）。
- **交付签收**：接受带可选章节号的 Methods/Results/References，避免临近预算误触发重写（#294 / #292）。
- **产物提交**：CAS ref commit 复用已校验对象元数据，降低长轨迹提交开销（#250；#230 仍开）。
- **真实 E2E 稳定化**：J5 等待托管 Python（#287 / #286）；主 Agent run 链完成后再做终局断言（#253）；中断时保留已完成旅程证据（#266 / #263）；Nightly flaky 断言（#207、#279）；L3 改为真实用户旅程（#272）。
- **CI 配套**：job 重跑覆盖同名 artifact（#302 / #301）；分数与诊断产物分离（#240）；Mock E2E 四 worker、UT 并行等（#273、#277、#268、#242）；Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 恢复进 daily/release，Nightly 结构化挂载 `science-research-team`（#270、#306）。

### 行为变更

- 启动不再强依赖本地沙箱可用；未就绪时执行被拒绝，需经恢复流程后再下发（#275）。
- Nightly Biomni 挂载 `science-research-team` 后，分数不可与 beta 裸题基线直接对比（#306）。

</details>

## 社区反馈

欢迎在本 Issue 讨论：

- 草案表述是否清楚、是否遗漏重要合入
- RC1 作为正式版前候选，你最关心的验证场景

请尽量附上复现步骤、日志或相关 PR/Issue 链接。

# English version

## Release positioning

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`**, like [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta), is a **pre-release ahead of the formal 0.3.0**. It builds on the existing JiuwenSwarm scientific workbench and continues to tighten quality and delivery engineering as a release candidate.

The previous version is `0.3.0-beta` (2026-09-30). This draft covers changes merged into `main` from **2026-10-01 through 2026-10-16** (Asia/Shanghai).

> This is a **community draft** for feedback, not a formal release announcement. The GitHub Release / tag will be published separately.

## Draft release notes

### New features

- **L1–L5 multi-level CI gates**: layered quality checks across PR → merge → daily → release, with Nightly/Release real E2E alongside hermetic checks (#259; related #280, #255, #258).

### Major fixes

- **Sandbox / Runner not ready**: decouple workbench startup from Runner readiness; execution remains fail-closed; the Agent can wait via `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` and present retry / switch / cancel recovery cards; distinguish “show waiting UI” from “authorize repair” (#275 / #265, #282).
- **Unparseable tool calls**: hold and recover during long research runs instead of misreporting a model-configuration error and killing the main or sub-Agent (#247 / #236).
- **Custom model settings**: keep provider presets when any settings request fails, avoiding a stuck empty Custom provider form (#288 / #281).
- **Deliverable acceptance**: accept Methods/Results/References headings with optional section numbers so near-budget rewrites are not triggered incorrectly (#294 / #292).
- **Artifact commits**: reuse validated object metadata on the CAS ref-commit path to cut long-trajectory commit cost (#250; #230 remains open).
- **Real E2E stabilization**: wait for managed Python on J5 (#287 / #286); assert only after the main Agent run chain completes (#253); retain completed-journey evidence on interrupt (#266 / #263); Nightly flaky assertions (#207, #279); L3 as real user journeys (#272).
- **CI follow-ups**: overwrite same-named artifacts on job re-run (#302 / #301); separate score and diagnostic artifacts (#240); Mock E2E four workers and UT parallelism (#273, #277, #268, #242); restore Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 to daily/release and structurally attach `science-research-team` on Nightly (#270, #306).

### Behavior changes

- Startup no longer requires a ready local sandbox; execution is rejected until recovery completes (#275).
- After Nightly Biomni attaches `science-research-team`, scores are not directly comparable to the beta bare-prompt baseline (#306).

Please comment on this issue with:

Include repro steps, logs, or related PR/issue links when possible.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

In multi-step science demos, the agent repeatedly hits **tool-call failures** that it then recovers from on retry. Tasks still complete, but the timeline fills with failed cards and wasted turns. Two concrete patterns showed up in Scenario 2/3.

## Repro / observations

### A. Specialist `task` missing required prompt (Scenario 2 Case B)

1. Create custom specialist **CSV质检专员** bound to skill `csv-quality-check`.
2. Start a session with that specialist selected; upload CSV; ask for a quality check **without** naming the skill.
3. Parent `read_skill` completes; first `task` **fails** (missing required prompt field); retry **completes** with `specialistId` and skill path.
4. Subagent eventually COMPLETED; parent re-checks and declares artifacts.

Session `378644b7-…`, project **自定义扩展演示**.

### B. lmfit `conf_interval` signature (Scenario 3 Case A)

1. Domain-allowlist sandbox; `environment_create` task env; `environment_install` lmfit **1.3.4** from PyPI.
2. Fit Michaelis–Menten; two `run_python` calls **fail** on lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention; later calls succeed after the agent fixes the call.
3. Final fit OK (Vmax/Km/R²), but timeline shows two failed Python cards.

Session `ae359b61-…`, project **科学计算演示**, 2026-10-16.

Similar soft failures also appeared in Scenario 1 (`run_shell` / `run_python` fail-then-complete).

## Expected

- Specialist delegation: first `task` payload should always include required fields (prompt) when the product launches a specialist subagent — schema/validation before the card is shown as failed.
- Scientific library helpers: either pin known-good call patterns in skills/examples, or catch common `conf_interval` / API mismatches with a clearer error that steers the next call without two opaque failures.
- Prefer failing closed in the UI with a one-line “retrying with fixed args” rather than raw failed tool cards as the default narrative.

## Actual

Runs complete via model self-repair, but users see multiple **failed** tool cards and longer wall time for routine fits / specialist handoffs.

## Priority

**Medium** — reliability / polish of the tool loop; not a hard blocker when Always-allow is on.

## Related

- #330 — engineering-heavy timeline makes these failures more alarming than they are
- #327 — long runs already lack incremental progress
items.title: [Bug]: Agent tool calls fail then recover mid-run (task missing prompt; lmfit conf_interval signature)

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

Uploading a PDF through the workspace **Drop files** control does not go through the paper-reader pipeline. Paper reader stays at **0 parsed**, and the agent only sees a raw file (often with almost no extractable scientific content unless it scrapes bytes itself).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, new session in a data-analysis project.
2. Drop `experiment_notes.pdf` (+ optional CSV) via **Drop files**.
3. Ask the agent to read the PDF notes and fit kinetics from the CSV (no network).
4. Observe: Paper reader counter remains **0 parsed**. Agent reports extracting only the single plain line from the PDF and explicitly notes missing protocol/units/replicates. Units come from the CSV header, not from structured paper parse.

Observed Scenario 1 Case B (session `c6372af5-…`, project **数据分析演示**), 2026-10-15.

## Expected

- Dropping a PDF into the workspace should either:
  - enqueue it for paper-reader parsing (same as the dedicated paper input), **or**
  - clearly label the upload as “file only / not paper-parsed” so users do not assume literature extraction ran.
- If Drop files is intentionally file-only, the empty/paper UI should not imply paper intake for that artifact.

## Actual

PDF is a workspace file only. Paper reader stays **0 parsed**. Structured literature extraction does not run on Drop-files PDFs.

## Priority

**Medium–High** for any “upload paper + analyze” flow; easy to misread as a successful paper ingest.

## Related

Not the same as empty-session CSV intro (#328). Speaks to intake path consistency between Drop files and paper-reader.
items.title: [Bug]: PDF uploaded via Drop files is not parsed by Paper reader (0 parsed)

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary

The workspace **Artifacts** list appears **project-scoped**: while working in session B, files from session A in the same project still show up (sometimes grouped under the other session’s name). Not a data-loss bug — the model still read the correct uploads — but the list is noisy and easy to mis-click.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 demos:

- Scenario 1: session B’s file count included session A artifacts.
- Scenario 2: during Specialist session, Case A reports still listed under “Skill csv-quality-check” while new files appeared under “Specialist CSV质检”.

## Why this may be intentional

Project-level sharing can be desirable (reuse a CSV across sessions, compare outputs). This issue is filed **low priority** to force an explicit product decision, not to demand an immediate change.

## Design questions (need a call)

1. Should Artifacts default to **current session only**, with an opt-in “Show project files”?
2. Or keep project scope but visually separate **This session** vs **Other sessions** with clearer hierarchy?
3. Should uploads be session-private by default and only promoted to project library on pin/share?

## Expected after a design pass

Whatever the choice, the panel should make scope obvious so users do not think another session’s outputs belong to the active run.

## Priority

**Low** — polish / information architecture; confirm against intended project-workspace model before changing.

## Related

Not a substitute for timeline density (#330).
items.title: Usability (low): workspace Artifacts panel is project-scoped and mixes other sessions’ files

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Problem

Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain literal `<think>` tags.

These tags appear as part of the visible title instead of a clean summary of the conversation. This makes session titles confusing and harder to scan.

The issue is intermittent; the exact trigger has not yet been identified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session and send a message.
2. Wait for the session title to be automatically generated.
3. Check the generated title.
4. Occasionally, the title contains literal `<think>` tags.

### Actual behavior

The generated session title includes `<think>` markup.

### Expected behavior

Automatically generated session titles should contain only a concise, readable summary of the conversation, without reasoning tags or reasoning content.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Automatically generated titles never display `<think>` or `</think>` tags.
- [ ] Reasoning content enclosed by these tags is excluded from the title.
- [ ] If no usable title remains after filtering, the application retains a safe default title.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes title-generation responses containing reasoning tags.
items.title: [Bug]: Automatically generated session titles occasionally contain `<think>` tags

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Problem

Users face two obstacles when downloading ScienceDiscovery:

1. **Release downloads are difficult to discover.** Installation packages are listed under **Assets** on the GitHub Releases page. When this section is collapsed, users may miss the downloads or struggle to find the package for their platform.
2. **The website installation page lacks a version selector and defaults to an outdated version.** Version 0.3 is available, but the installation page still defaults to 0.2. Users cannot select a release version directly on the page and may install an older version unintentionally.

### Proposed improvements

**GitHub Releases**

- Add a clearly visible download section to each release description, with direct links to installation packages.
- Label each download by operating system and architecture so users can identify the appropriate package without expanding Assets.

**Website installation page**

- Add a version selector so users can choose between available releases.
- Default to the latest stable release, currently 0.3.
- Keep download links and installation commands consistent with the selected version.
- Update the default version when a new stable release becomes available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can find installation package links in the release description without expanding Assets.
- [ ] Download links clearly identify the supported operating system and architecture.
- [ ] The website installation page provides a version selector.
- [ ] The installation page defaults to the latest stable release.
- [ ] Download links and installation commands match the selected version.
- [ ] Publishing a new stable release updates the website’s default installation version.
items.title: [Bug]: Release downloads are hard to find and the website installation page defaults to an outdated version

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_
items.title: [Feature]: Natural-language program evolution: turn /evolve-design from a hidden slash command into a framework-recommended, natural-language interaction

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What is wrong

On a large screen the artifact viewer is still a small card. It is the dialog opened from an artifact (`artifact-modal-panel` in `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css`):

- width `min(1080px, 100%)`
- only a max height, `calc(100vh - 56px)`, so a short file stays as short as its content

On a 1920px-wide window that width is about 56% of the viewport. On a 2560px window it is about 42%. Plots, tables, notebooks, and source previews then sit in a column that does not use the screen the user is looking at.

The same class is the shell for the evidence viewer and the node-detail viewer (`ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, `EvidenceModal.tsx`, `DetailModal.tsx`). They should grow with it. Confirmation dialogs and settings panels use other classes and stay small.

## What a reasonable size is

A decision dialog and a content viewer are different objects.

- Material’s dialog cap (560dp wide, 48dp from the screen edge) is for a question or a confirmation. Applying it here would make the viewer smaller.
- A content viewer should take most of the viewport and leave a visible margin, so the dimmed page and the click-outside close still read as a layer. A hard pixel cap still matters on a 4K display, or a paragraph becomes one very long line.
- WorkBuddy opens an artifact as a tab in the right-hand pane, and that pane can go fullscreen. This product’s right pane is 390px, which is too narrow to become the viewer. Growing the existing dialog is the change; do not move artifact viewing into that pane.
- This repo already treats specialized viewers as large windows: the CSV workspace is `min(1480px, 97vw)` by `min(920px, 95vh)` (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/styles.css`), and the molecule window is `min(1360px, 96vw)` by `min(880px, 93vh)`. The generic artifact dialog is the one that did not follow that pattern.

## Target

On a wide screen, size the artifact viewer like those content windows, one step larger:

- width `min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`
- height `min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`

That is 1600×960 when the window is large enough, and it shrinks with an 80px total margin when it is not. It does not go edge to edge. At `max-width: 900px` the existing rule already makes this panel full viewport; leave that rule alone.

Inside the window, prose stays readable. Markdown body copy keeps a measure of about 76ch. Tables, code, images, and plots use the window width. Do not widen a paragraph to 1600px.

The evidence title already ellipsizes at `min(560px, 60vw)`. That cap can stay. The comment above it still says the panel is about 1080px; update the comment if that block is touched.

## Out of scope

- Settings, creation, and deletion dialogs.
- The CSV workspace and the molecule window. They are already larger than 1080px.
- The 390px workspace panel.
- The conversation column width.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width of about 1920px, the artifact viewer is 1600px wide and 960px tall, centered, with the page still visible around it.
- At a width between 900px and 1600px, the viewer is the viewport minus about 80px, not stuck at 1080px.
- At 900px and below, the viewer is still the full viewport, as it is today.
- A markdown artifact’s paragraphs do not run the full 1600px. A wide table or source preview does use the window.
- Evidence and node-detail viewers use the same size. A settings dialog does not.
- A render test, or a CSS assertion next to the existing dialog styles, locks the new width and height.
items.title: [Feature]: Make the artifact viewer use a large screen

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What to change

On a large screen the Session conversation is too narrow, and it sits on the left. The composer under it is a different width. User messages should be a bubble on the right.

This is layout only. Do not change what a message contains, the right-hand artifact panel, or the narrow-screen stacking behavior.

## Current layout

The conversation pane is the left track of `.content-grid` (`apps/web/src/styles/conversation.css`). The right track is a fixed 390px panel.

Inside the conversation pane:

- Each `.message` and the run timeline are capped at `820px` and are not centered, so on a wide pane they stay on the left. The same `820px` cap is repeated for the message skeleton, process records, and several timeline blocks (`conversation.css`, `timeline.css`, `process-records.css`, `feedback.css`).
- The composer does not use that cap. It stretches across the pane with `margin: 0 max(28px, 5vw) 28px`, so on a large screen it is wider than the transcript above it.
- A user turn is the same left grid as an assistant turn: a 40px avatar column, then the body. `.message.user .markdown-body` is only an inline block with a sunk background. It is not on the right.

## What other agents do

Public pages do not publish a single official pixel width. The pattern that matches this request:

- **Doubao (doubao.com).** The transcript and the input share one centered column (`--center-content-max-width`, `--content-max-width`, `--chat-area-max-width` on the chat route). The column stays centered in the area beside the left navigation as the window grows; it is not the full window. User sends are a separate right-aligned bubble. Community style scripts refer to a stock send-message cap around `max-w-650`, and they right-align that bubble with `margin-left: auto`. The stock column is what people widen with userscripts; one width slider starts at 760px, another forces 1600px. Those overrides are “make it full width,” which is not what we want. A public recreation of the Doubao column uses `max-width: 1000px`.
- **WorkBuddy.** The published UI is a left task list, a center conversation, and an optional right results panel. The input sits at the bottom of that same center column, so the transcript and the input are one width. The docs do not give a pixel width or say which side a user message sits on.
- **Trae.** Side chat is the IDE panel on the right (Command+U / Ctrl+U). Its width is the panel the user drags, not a centered reading column. It is a poor template for this screen.

## Target

On a wide conversation pane, one centered column holds the transcript and the composer. Make it a little wider than 820px, and do not let it fill the pane.

Use **1000px** as the shared max width (`min(1000px, 100%)`, centered with `margin-inline: auto`). That is the modest step implied by “a little wider,” and it matches the 1000px Doubao-style column rather than the 1600px full-width userscripts. Put the number in one custom property and point the transcript, timeline, process records, skeleton, and composer at it, so the old `820px` copies cannot drift apart.

The composer’s outer width is that column. Its inner padding can stay. Short viewports keep today’s full-width behavior, including the ~900px case where the sidebar must not cover the conversation.

User messages, inside that column:

- The bubble sits on the right.
- A short message is only as wide as its text. A long message wraps and may use the column width, but it still starts from the right.
- Assistant replies stay on the left and use the column width.
- Do not leave the user avatar in the left gutter while the bubble is on the right. Keep the avatar with the bubble, or drop the user avatar if it fights the bubble. Assistant avatars stay on the left.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width where the conversation pane is clearly wider than 1000px, the transcript and the composer are the same width, centered in the pane, and that width is 1000px rather than 820px or the full pane.
- A short user message is a bubble on the right of that column. An assistant message stays on the left.
- Below the width of the column, the column fills the pane and the composer still matches it. The existing narrow layout, including the sidebar at about 900px, still fits on the first screen.
- The right artifact panel stays 390px.
- A Web layout test or the existing conversation render test covers the shared column and the right-aligned user bubble.
items.title: [Feature]: Center a wider conversation column and right-align user bubbles

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Motivation

Currently, every conversation must belong to a project, and creating a project requires too much configuration before users can start chatting.

This adds friction to the first interaction: users who simply want to ask a question or explore an idea must first create and configure a project, even when they do not yet need one. It also encourages creating projects for one-off conversations, making project management unnecessarily cluttered.

Users should be able to open the application and start a conversation immediately, then organize their work into projects when needed.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make project membership optional for conversations.**
   - Provide a prominent “New chat” entry that works without creating or selecting a project.
   - Support standalone conversations for quick questions, exploration, and one-off tasks.
   - Keep project-based conversations available for ongoing research and related work.

2. **Allow users to organize conversations into projects later.**
   - Let users move a standalone conversation into a new or existing project.
   - Preserve conversation history and associated artifacts when moving it.
   - Make it clear whether a conversation belongs to a project.

3. **Simplify project creation.**
   - Require only the minimum information needed to create a project, such as its name.
   - Provide sensible defaults and make advanced configuration optional.
   - Allow users to update project settings later instead of requiring them before the first conversation.

4. **Provide clear navigation for both workflows.**
   - Make standalone conversations and projects easy to find.
   - Let users start a conversation directly from the main interface.
   - Within a project, let users create conversations associated with that project.

## Example user flows

### Start chatting immediately

Open the application → New chat → Send a message.

No project creation or project configuration is required.

### Organize an exploratory conversation

Start a standalone conversation → Decide to continue the work → Move the conversation into a new or existing project.

### Start with a project

Create a project with minimal information → Start a conversation → Configure additional project settings when needed.

## Questions to settle

- Should standalone conversations remain in chat history by default, with an explicitly ephemeral mode handled separately?
- Which project settings can use defaults, and which are genuinely required before a project-specific capability runs?
- When an existing conversation moves into a project, how should project context and settings apply to subsequent messages?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with no projects can open the application and send a first message without creating or configuring a project.
- [ ] Users can create and continue conversations outside projects.
- [ ] Users can still create conversations directly within a project.
- [ ] A standalone conversation can be moved into a new or existing project without losing its history or associated artifacts.
- [ ] Project creation requires only minimal information; advanced settings can be configured later.
- [ ] Navigation clearly distinguishes standalone conversations from project conversations.
- [ ] Existing projects and their conversations remain accessible.
- [ ] E2E coverage verifies starting a conversation with no projects, creating a project with minimal input, and moving a standalone conversation into a project.
items.title: [Feature]: Allow conversations outside projects and simplify project creation

## Environment

- Release package `sciencediscovery` **0.3.0-beta** (x86_64), Linux, web UI

## Symptom

On the left-side project panel, the **collapse** control has no effect: clicking it does not hide the projects listed below, and the panel's expanded/collapsed state does not change.

## Repro

1. Open the web UI.
2. Look at the left-side project panel.
3. Click its collapse control.
4. Expected: the list of projects under the panel is hidden / the panel folds.
5. Actual: the list stays visible, no state change.

## Note

The same UI has working collapse/expand controls for other sections — `memory.action.collapseAll` / `expandAll`, `mcp.collapseServer` / `expandServer`, `artifact.collapseRunOutputs` / `expandRunOutputs`, and the file/skill sidebars (`收起包文件侧栏`, `收起 Skill 侧栏`). Only the project panel's toggle appears not to apply its state. Comparing its click handler / state binding to those working sidebars should make the difference easy to find.
